# `mosaics-spectrum` — 1D Spectrum Extraction

`mosaics-spectrum` (`uv run -m mosaics.cli.spectrum`) downloads variable-length 1D spectra across spectroscopic surveys and stores them as parallel Arrow `large_list` columns (`{slug}_flux`, `{slug}_error`, `{slug}_wavelength`, `{slug}_mask`) in a Lance dataset.

## Subcommands

- `full`: Fetch spectra across multiple spectroscopic surveys defined in `--config` (`defs/full.yaml`) into a single Lance dataset.
- Per-survey subcommands (`2dfgrs`, `6dfgs`, `desi1`, `euclidq1`, `hasp`, `lamost11`, `sdss17`): Fetch spectra for a single spectroscopic survey using its configured adapter(s).

## Examples

```console
$ uv run -m mosaics.cli.spectrum sdss17 -t test/objects_sample_1k.csv -o sdss17_spectra.lance --snr-floor 2.0
$ uv run -m mosaics.cli.spectrum desi1 -t test/objects_sample_1k.csv -o desi1_spectra.lance --via healpix
$ uv run -m mosaics.cli.spectrum full -t test/objects_sample_1k.csv -o spectra_full.lance --config defs/full.yaml --snr-floor 2.0
```

## Command-line reference

<!-- generated:cli-spectrum -->
**Entry points:** `mosaics-spectrum` or `uv run -m mosaics.cli.spectrum`

### Top-level options

```text
mosaics.cli.spectrum [-h]
                            {2dfgrs,6dfgs,desi1,euclidq1,hasp,lamost11,sdss17,url,template,full}
                            ...
```

### `mosaics-spectrum 2dfgrs`

2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey spectra, via template.

```text
mosaics.cli.spectrum 2dfgrs [-h] --targets TARGETS [--ra-col RA_COLUMN]
                                   [--dec-col DEC_COLUMN] [--id-col ID_COLUMN]
                                   [--limit LIMIT] [--sort {native,key}]
                                   [--key-col KEY_COLUMNS [KEY_COLUMNS ...]]
                                   [--url-template URL_TEMPLATE]
                                   [--format {desi,fits,generic,hasp,lamost,sdss,votable}]
                                   [--prefix PREFIX]
                                   [--arrays {flux,error,wavelength,mask} [{flux,error,wavelength,mask} ...]]
                                   --output OUTPUT [--dtype DTYPE]
                                   [--max-samples MAX_SAMPLES]
                                   [--snr-floor SNR_FLOOR] [--resume]
                                   [--no-stats] [--retry-failed]
                                   [--proxy PROXY]
                                   [--max-per-origin MAX_PER_ORIGIN]
                                   [--retries RETRIES] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                                   [--proxy-stats-url URL] [--wandb]
                                   [--wandb-project WANDB_PROJECT]
                                   [--wandb-entity WANDB_ENTITY]
                                   [--wandb-name WANDB_NAME]
                                   [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE] [--no-progress]
                                   [--log-level {DEBUG,INFO,WARNING,ERROR,CRITICAL}]
                                   [--status-interval STATUS_INTERVAL]
                                   [--option KEY=VALUE]
```

| Option / Argument | Default | Choices | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--targets`, `-t` `TARGETS` | *required* | — | Target table (parquet, csv, fits, ...) listing the spectra to fetch. |
| `--ra-col` `RA_COLUMN` | `None` | — | Right ascension column, recorded in the failure sidecar. Optional. |
| `--dec-col` `DEC_COLUMN` | `None` | — | Declination column, recorded in the failure sidecar. Optional. |
| `--id-col` `ID_COLUMN` | `None` | — | Unique row key used to resume. Synthesised from the row index if omitted. |
| `--limit` `LIMIT` | `None` | — | Process at most this many targets. |
| `--sort` `SORT` | `native` | `native`, `key` | Target order. 'key' groups spectra that share a remote file, which is what makes desi-healpix affordable. Default: native. |
| `--key-col` `KEY_COLUMNS` | `None` | — | Columns identifying a spectrum. Defaults to whatever the chosen backend needs, so this is only for a table that names them unusually. |
| `--url-template` `URL_TEMPLATE` | `None` | — | Format string built from target-table columns, or one of: 2dfgrs, lamost-dr11, sdss-eboss, sdss-legacy, sdss-v. |
| `--format` `FMT` | `None` | `desi`, `fits`, `generic`, `hasp`, `lamost`, `sdss`, `votable` | Reader used to decode a response. Defaults to the source's own. |
| `--prefix` `PREFIX` | `None` | — | Column-name prefix, e.g. "sdss" gives sdss_flux. Defaults to the source name. |
| `--arrays` `ARRAYS` | `None` | `flux`, `error`, `wavelength`, `mask` | Which of a spectrum's arrays to store. Defaults to the source's own set. |
| `--output`, `-o` `OUTPUT` | *required* | — | Destination Lance dataset. |
| `--dtype` `DTYPE` | `float32` | — | Sample dtype. Default: float32. |
| `--max-samples` `MAX_SAMPLES` | `2000000` | — | Reject a spectrum longer than this. Default: 2000000. |
| `--snr-floor` `SNR_FLOOR` | `3.0` | — | Signal-to-noise a sample must reach to be marked usable in the mask, where the survey publishes an error (default: 3). Worth lowering: at 3 the mask excludes most of a faint object's continuum, so a model trained on the mask sees little but emission lines. The value used is recorded in the dataset metadata. |
| `--resume` | `false` | — | Continue an existing dataset, skipping spectra already present. |
| `--no-stats` | `true` | — | Skip the QA metric columns. Makes resume read samples instead. |
| `--retry-failed` | `false` | — | With --resume, fetch again the spectra recorded in the failure sidecar. |
| `--proxy` `PROXY` | `None` | — | Proxy URL, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8888 to route through a mosaics proxy pool. HTTPS_PROXY is honoured when this is omitted. |
| `--max-per-origin` `MAX_PER_ORIGIN` | `3` | — | In-flight requests per host per source IP, which is what an archive actually throttles on. Behind a proxy pool the real ceiling is this times the number of connected workers, read from --proxy-stats-url. Default: 3. |
| `--retries` `RETRIES` | `5` | — | Attempts per request. Only transient failures consume attempts; a 404 fails immediately. Default: 5. |
| `--timeout` `TIMEOUT` | `60.0` | — | Per-request timeout in seconds. Default: 60.0. |
| `--proxy-stats-url` `URL` | `None` | — | URL of a mosaics proxy stats endpoint, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8889/stats. Read once at startup to learn how many workers are connected, which is what turns --max-per-origin into the real per-host ceiling, and polled per batch for the telemetry panel when --wandb is on. A proxy that cannot be reached is treated as a single source IP. |
| `--wandb` | `false` | — | Log progress to W&B. |
| `--wandb-project` `WANDB_PROJECT` | `None` | — | W&B project. |
| `--wandb-entity` `WANDB_ENTITY` | `None` | — | W&B entity. |
| `--wandb-name` `WANDB_NAME` | `None` | — | W&B run name. |
| `--batch-size`, `-b` `BATCH_SIZE` | `512` | — | Spectra per download-and-append cycle. Default: 512. |
| `--no-progress` | `true` | — | Hide the progress bar. |
| `--log-level` `LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL` | Logging verbosity. |
| `--status-interval` `STATUS_INTERVAL` | `30.0` | — | Seconds between [PIPELINE STATUS] blocks, which say how many batches are done and which backends are in flight. A backend can be silent for minutes behind a rate limit, so this is what tells a quiet run from a stuck one. 0 turns them off. Default: 30. |
| `--option` `KEY=VALUE` | `[]` | — | Backend option override, repeatable. Escape hatch over a preset. |

### `mosaics-spectrum 6dfgs`

6dF Galaxy Survey DR3 spectra, via url.

```text
mosaics.cli.spectrum 6dfgs [-h] --targets TARGETS [--ra-col RA_COLUMN]
                                  [--dec-col DEC_COLUMN] [--id-col ID_COLUMN]
                                  [--limit LIMIT] [--sort {native,key}]
                                  [--key-col KEY_COLUMNS [KEY_COLUMNS ...]]
                                  [--url-column URL_COLUMN]
                                  [--format {desi,fits,generic,hasp,lamost,sdss,votable}]
                                  [--prefix PREFIX]
                                  [--arrays {flux,error,wavelength,mask} [{flux,error,wavelength,mask} ...]]
                                  --output OUTPUT [--dtype DTYPE]
                                  [--max-samples MAX_SAMPLES]
                                  [--snr-floor SNR_FLOOR] [--resume]
                                  [--no-stats] [--retry-failed]
                                  [--proxy PROXY]

                                  [--wandb-entity WANDB_ENTITY]

                                  [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE] [--no-progress]
                                  [--log-level {DEBUG,INFO,WARNING,ERROR,CRITICAL}]
                                  [--status-interval STATUS_INTERVAL]
                                  [--option KEY=VALUE]
```

```text
mosaics.cli.spectrum desi1 [-h] --targets TARGETS [--ra-col RA_COLUMN]

                                  [--id-column SPARCL_ID_COLUMN]
                                  [--prefix PREFIX]
                                  [--arrays {flux,error,wavelength,mask} [{flux,error,wavelength,mask} ...]]
                                  --output OUTPUT [--dtype DTYPE]

                                  [--wandb-name WANDB_NAME]
                                  [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE] [--no-progress]
                                  [--log-level {DEBUG,INFO,WARNING,ERROR,CRITICAL}]
                                  [--status-interval STATUS_INTERVAL]
                                  [--option KEY=VALUE]
```

| Option / Argument | Default | Choices | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--targets`, `-t` `TARGETS` | *required* | — | Target table (parquet, csv, fits, ...) listing the spectra to fetch. |

| `--dataset` `DATASET` | `DESI-DR1` | — | SPARCL dataset. Default: DESI-DR1. |

| `--prefix` `PREFIX` | `None` | — | Column-name prefix, e.g. "sdss" gives sdss_flux. Defaults to the source name. |
| `--arrays` `ARRAYS` | `None` | `flux`, `error`, `wavelength`, `mask` | Which of a spectrum's arrays to store. Defaults to the source's own set. |

Worth lowering: at 3 the mask excludes most of a faint object's continuum, so a model trained on the mask sees little but emission lines. The value used is recorded in the dataset metadata. |
| `--resume` | `false` | — | Continue an existing dataset, skipping spectra already present. |
| `--no-stats` | `true` | — | Skip the QA metric columns. Makes resume read samples instead. |
| `--retry-failed` | `false` | — | With --resume, fetch again the spectra recorded in the failure sidecar. |
| `--proxy` `PROXY` | `None` | — | Proxy URL, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8888 to route through a mosaics proxy pool. HTTPS_PROXY is honoured when this is omitted. |
| `--max-per-origin` `MAX_PER_ORIGIN` | `2` | — | In-flight requests per host per source IP, which is what an archive actually throttles on. Behind a proxy pool the real ceiling is this times the number of connected workers, read from --proxy-stats-url. Default: 3. |
| `--retries` `RETRIES` | `5` | — | Attempts per request. Only transient failures consume attempts; a 404 fails immediately. Default: 5. |
| `--timeout` `TIMEOUT` | `1800.0` | — | Per-request timeout in seconds. Default: 60.0. |
| `--proxy-stats-url` `URL` | `None` | — | URL of a mosaics proxy stats endpoint, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8889/stats. Read once at startup to learn how many workers are connected, which is what turns --max-per-origin into the real per-host ceiling, and polled per batch for the telemetry panel when --wandb is on. | `--log-level` `LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL` | Logging verbosity. |

| `--proxy` `PROXY` | `None` | — | Proxy URL, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8888 to route through a mosaics proxy pool. HTTPS_PROXY is honoured when this is omitted. |
| `--max-per-origin` `MAX_PER_ORIGIN` | `3` | — | In-flight requests per host per source IP, which is what an archive actually throttles on. Behind a proxy pool the real ceiling is this times the number of connected workers, read from --proxy-stats-url. Default: 3. |
| `--retries` `RETRIES` | `5` | — | Attempts per request. Only transient failures consume attempts; a 404 fails immediately. Default: 5. |
| `--timeout` `TIMEOUT` | `60.0` | — | Per-request timeout in seconds. Default: 60.0. |
| `--proxy-stats-url` `URL` | `None` | — | URL of a mosaics proxy stats endpoint, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8889/stats. Read once at startup to learn how many workers are connected, which is what turns --max-per-origin into the real per-host ceiling, and polled per batch for the telemetry panel when --wandb is on. A proxy that cannot be reached is treated as a single source IP. |
| `--wandb` | `false` | — | Log progress to W&B. |
| `--wandb-project` `WANDB_PROJECT` | `None` | — | W&B project. |
| `--wandb-entity` `WANDB_ENTITY` | `None` | — | W&B entity. |
| `--wandb-name` `WANDB_NAME` | `None` | — | W&B run name. |
| `--batch-size`, `-b` `BATCH_SIZE` | `512` | — | Spectra per download-and-append cycle. Default: 512. |
| `--no-progress` | `true` | — | Hide the progress bar. |
| `--log-level` `LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL` | Logging verbosity. |
| `--status-interval` `STATUS_INTERVAL` | `30.0` | — | Seconds between [PIPELINE STATUS] blocks, which say how many batches are done and which backends are in flight. A backend can be silent for minutes behind a rate limit, so this is what tells a quiet run from a stuck one. 0 turns them off. Default: 30. |
| `--option` `KEY=VALUE` | `[]` | — | Backend option override, repeatable. Escape hatch over a preset. |

### `mosaics-spectrum lamost11`

LAMOST DR11 MRS spectra, via template.

```text
mosaics.cli.spectrum lamost11 [-h] --targets TARGETS
                                     [--ra-col RA_COLUMN]
                                     [--dec-col DEC_COLUMN]
                                     [--id-col ID_COLUMN] [--limit LIMIT]
                                     [--sort {native,key}]
                                     [--key-col KEY_COLUMNS [KEY_COLUMNS ...]]
                                     [--url-template URL_TEMPLATE]
                                     [--format {desi,fits,generic,hasp,lamost,sdss,votable}]
                                     [--prefix PREFIX]
                                     [--arrays {flux,error,wavelength,mask} [{flux,error,wavelength,mask} ...]]
                                     --output OUTPUT [--dtype DTYPE]
                                     [--max-samples MAX_SAMPLES]
                                     [--snr-floor SNR_FLOOR] [--resume]
                                     [--no-stats] [--retry-failed]
                                     [--proxy PROXY]
                                     [--max-per-origin MAX_PER_ORIGIN]
                                     [--retries RETRIES] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                                     [--proxy-stats-url URL] [--wandb]
                                     [--wandb-project WANDB_PROJECT]
                                     [--wandb-entity WANDB_ENTITY]
                                     [--wandb-name WANDB_NAME]
                                     [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE] [--no-progress]
                                     [--log-level {DEBUG,INFO,WARNING,ERROR,CRITICAL}]
                                     [--status-interval STATUS_INTERVAL]
                                     [--option KEY=VALUE]
```

| Option / Argument | Default | Choices | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--targets`, `-t` `TARGETS` | *required* | — | Target table (parquet, csv, fits, ...) listing the spectra to fetch. |
| `--ra-col` `RA_COLUMN` | `None` | — | Right ascension column, recorded in the failure sidecar. Optional. |
| `--dec-col` `DEC_COLUMN` | `None` | — | Declination column, recorded in the failure sidecar. Optional. |
| `--id-col` `ID_COLUMN` | `None` | — | Unique row key used to resume. Synthesised from the row index if omitted. |
| `--limit` `LIMIT` | `None` | — | Process at most this many targets. |
| `--sort` `SORT` | `native` | `native`, `key` | Target order. 'key' groups spectra that share a remote file, which is what makes desi-healpix affordable. Default: native. |
| `--key-col` `KEY_COLUMNS` | `None` | — | Columns identifying a spectrum. Defaults to whatever the chosen backend needs, so this is only for a table that names them unusually. |
| `--url-template` `URL_TEMPLATE` | `None` | — | Format string built from target-table columns, or one of: 2dfgrs, lamost-dr11, sdss-eboss, sdss-legacy, sdss-v. |
| `--format` `FMT` | `None` | `desi`, `fits`, `generic`, `hasp`, `lamost`, `sdss`, `votable` | Reader used to decode a response. Defaults to the source's own. |
| `--prefix` `PREFIX` | `None` | — | Column-name prefix, e.g. "sdss" gives sdss_flux. Defaults to the source name. |
| `--arrays` `ARRAYS` | `None` | `flux`, `error`, `wavelength`, `mask` | Which of a spectrum's arrays to store. Defaults to the source's own set. |
| `--output`, `-o` `OUTPUT` | *required* | — | Destination Lance dataset. |
| `--dtype` `DTYPE` | `float32` | — | Sample dtype. Default: float32. |
| `--max-samples` `MAX_SAMPLES` | `2000000` | — | Reject a spectrum longer than this. Default: 2000000. |
| `--snr-floor` `SNR_FLOOR` | `3.0` | — | Signal-to-noise a sample must reach to be marked usable in the mask, where the survey publishes an error (default: 3). Worth lowering: at 3 the mask excludes most of a faint object's continuum, so a model trained on the mask sees little but emission lines. The value used is recorded in the dataset metadata. |
| `--resume` | `false` | — | Continue an existing dataset, skipping spectra already present. |
| `--no-stats` | `true` | — | Skip the QA metric columns. Makes resume read samples instead. |
| `--retry-failed` | `false` | — | With --resume, fetch again the spectra recorded in the failure sidecar. |

Read once at startup to learn how many workers are connected, which is what turns --max-per-origin into the real per-host ceiling, and polled per batch for the telemetry panel when --wandb is on. A proxy that cannot be reached is treated as a single source IP. |
| `--wandb` | `false` | — | Log progress to W&B. |
| `--wandb-project` `WANDB_PROJECT` | `None` | — | W&B project. |
| `--wandb-entity` `WANDB_ENTITY` | `None` | — | W&B entity. |

### `mosaics-spectrum full`

Fetch several surveys for one target list into one dataset.

```text

                                 [--wandb-entity WANDB_ENTITY]
                                 [--wandb-name WANDB_NAME]
                                 [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE] [--no-progress]
                                 [--log-level {DEBUG,INFO,WARNING,ERROR,CRITICAL}]
                                 [--status-interval STATUS_INTERVAL]
                                 [--option KEY=VALUE]
```

| Option / Argument | Default | Choices | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--targets`, `-t` `TARGETS` | *required* | — | Target table (parquet, csv, fits, ...) listing the spectra to fetch. |

| `--dec-col` `DEC_COLUMN` | `None` | — | Declination column, recorded in the failure sidecar. Optional. |

| `--config`, `-c` `FILE` | `None` | — | Survey definitions entrypoint, describing the surveys and, per survey, the adapter that fills its columns. # `mosaics-targets` — Multi-Survey Target Selection & Crossmatch Pipeline

`mosaics-targets` (`uv run -m mosaics.cli.targets`) executes the eight-stage target selection, photometric rescue, multi-survey crossmatch, homogenisation, and reporting pipeline over the declination sky-cell grid.

## Key capabilities

- Reads all survey roles, SQL queries, HATS paths, column maps, and photometric/spectroscopic systems from `--config` (default `defs/full.yaml`; production runs typically use `defs/targets.yaml`).
- Stores intermediate sky-cell datasets under `<output>/stores/` with append-only cell ledgers so re-running the same command resumes automatically from unfinished sky cells.
- Writes `<output>/targets_report.yaml` and renders the `mosaics-targets@1` `scireport` bundle (`<output>/report/targets_report.scireport.zip`), chapter-split Markdown (`<output>/report/md/`), and PDF (`<output>/report/pdf/report.pdf`).

## Examples

```console
$ uv run -m mosaics.cli.targets --config defs/targets.yaml -o ./targets_run --dec-range 0.0 1.0 --plan plan.yaml
$ uv run -m mosaics.cli.targets --config defs/targets.yaml -o ./targets_run --dec-range 0.0 1.0 --workers 8
$ uv run -m mosaics.cli.targets --config defs/targets.yaml -o ./targets_run --dec-range -5.0 5.0 --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8888
```

| `--config`, `-c` `FILE` | `None` | — | Survey definitions entrypoint. Everything this run knows about a survey comes from the files it pulls in: which query extracts it, which table it crossmatches against, which passbands it measures through and how its brightnesses convert. Point it at a smaller entrypoint, or pass --survey, to run a subset of the surveys. Default: full.yaml under defs/, which is every survey. |
| `--survey` `REF` | `None` | — | Survey files to run on, replacing the entrypoint's `surveys:`: library names or paths, `.yaml` optional, globs allowed (`--survey surveys/ls11 surveys/wise`). The entrypoint's `overrides:` still apply. |

| `--overwrite` | `false` | — | Rebuild artifacts that already exist instead of reusing them. Off by default: extraction is the expensive part of the run, and a re-run usually means "add a survey" or "widen the box", not "start again". |
| `--overwrite-cache` | `false` | — | Replace every sky-cell store this run reads -- its rows and its ledger of finished and failed cells -- and fetch it again. Not implied by --overwrite, which rebuilds the candidate table and the catalogue from the stores already on disk: that costs minutes and contacts no archive, refetching costs the hours the stores exist to avoid. Pass this when an archive has republished its data. |

| `--store-dir` `STORE_DIR` | `None` | — | Where each extraction and crossmatch keeps its rows: one Lance dataset per step, kept by HEALPix cell beside a ledger of finished and failed cells. A later run over a wider --ra-range or --dec-range fetches only the cells it does not have yet, and a run that crashed fetches only the cells it had not finished. Defaults to a "store" directory under --output. Nothing here is evicted; see --prune-stores. |
| `--files-dir` `FILES_DIR` | `None` | — | Where a survey queried on this machine keeps the catalogue it downloads -- SDSS specObj, the 2MASS extended source catalogue -- as one Parquet file per table. Downloaded once and shared by dry and real runs; only --overwrite-cache fetches it again, and --prune-stores never deletes it. The Legacy Survey sweeps downloaded from NERSC, converted, and their position index, are kept here too, under sweep/. Defaults to a "files" directory under --output. |
| `--brick-cache-size` `BRICK_CACHE_SIZE` | `200.0` | — | Disk budget, in GiB, of the Legacy Survey catalogue files kept under --files-dir: each sweep downloaded from NERSC and converted to Parquet. Past it files are evicted least recently used, and one needed again is downloaded again. A cell at the default order is a 1.83 degree pixel and selects a handful of the 5-degree sweeps, so leave room for the sweeps the cells around it reach too. Default: 200. |
| `--catalog-mode` `CATALOG_MODE` | `materialise` | `materialise`, `view` | What target_catalog is. "materialise" (the default) writes every column of every row into target_catalog.lance -- a third physical copy of values the stores already hold, and the one a reader can open knowing nothing about this pipeline. "view" writes target_catalog.view/ instead: the query that rebuilds the catalogue from the stores, beside the only thing that cannot be rebuilt -- what the cleaning decided, which is the deduplication survivors, the field of view and the split labels. It costs a join when the catalogue is read and saves the copy. It cannot be combined with --prune-stores, which would delete what the query reads. |
| `--prune-stores` | `false` | — | Delete the stores this run read once target_catalog.lance and targets_report.yaml are written, to reclaim their disk. The next run fetches every cell again, so leave this off while widening --dec-range step by step. |
| `--scratch-dir` `SCRATCH_DIR` | `None` | — | Where DuckDB spills and the phases put their intermediate tables. Wiped at the start and end of every phase that uses it, so nothing here survives the run -- this is the opposite of --store-dir. Defaults to sitting beside each artifact. Point it at a large disk: the deduplication copies every row into each neighbouring sky tile and DuckDB spills its sorts here too. The nersc provider also downloads and converts each Legacy Survey sweep here before it enters --files-dir, so where the output is on NFS this wants to be a local disk. |
| `--plan` `PLAN` | `None` | — | Write the execution plan to this YAML file and exit without running. Constructs no provider, so it never logs in. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | — | Run the whole graph against a small slice of every source, writing to <output>/dry_run so it cannot be mistaken for a real catalogue. |
| `--dry-run-rows` `DRY_RUN_ROWS` | `10000` | — | Rows a dry run caps each extraction at. Default: 10000. |
| `--strict` | `false` | — | Abort the run if a crossmatch fails after its retries. By default a failed archive is recorded and skipped, and the run goes on to build the catalogue without that survey. Use this when an incomplete catalogue is not worth having. |
| `--retry-failed` `RETRY_FAILED` | `none` | `none`, `band`, `all` | Fetch again the sky cells an earlier run recorded as failed. Bare, or as "band", it retries the failures inside this run's --ra-range and --dec-range. As "all" it retries every failure ever ledgered, wherever in the sky it is -- a cell is a global identifier, so a failure recorded by one run is retryable by any other, and those cells are stored but do not join this run's catalogue. "all" is opt-in because widening the bare flag to mean it would make a narrow run drag in the whole sky's backlog. Without the flag a failed cell stays out of the catalogue and the plan lists it, so one bad patch of an archive does not cost a rerun of everything around it. |
| `--dec-range` `DEC_MIN DEC_MAX` | `None` | — | Restrict every extraction to this declination band, in degrees. The way to try a real run at a size worth waiting for: unlike --dry-run, a band is a coherent piece of sky that the photometry and the spectroscopy both cover, so the joins downstream actually match. Combine with --ra-range for a box. Default: the whole sky. |
| `--ra-range` `RA_MIN RA_MAX` | `None` | — | Restrict every extraction to this right ascension wedge, in degrees. RA_MIN greater than RA_MAX is a wedge across RA 0, so "--ra-range 350 10" is the twenty degrees around it. Cells are HEALPix pixels bounded in both axes, so a run over a box reuses every cell an earlier run fetched and a later, wider run fetches only what it lacks -- in either axis. Default: the whole circle. |
| `--xmatch-radius` `XMATCH_RADIUS` | `None` | — | One radius for every match: a spectrum belongs to a photometric object within it, and every crossmatch uses it in place of its survey's own `crossmatch.radius`. A bare number is arcsec. Default: each survey's own radius, and 1.0 arcsec for the spectrum-to-photometry match, the rescue and a survey with no crossmatch section. |
| `--hle` | `false` | — | Size every cutout with the half-light-ellipse method alone: the half-light radius times the circle correction factor of the r magnitude is the semi-major axis of the ellipse that ls11_shape_e1 and ls11_shape_e2 describe (axis ratio (1-e)/(1+e)), and the larger side of its bounding box is the catalogue's `fov`. By default the ellipse form is used, and the circle form where the ellipse is missing. Either way a row with a missing measurement is left out of the catalogue, and a row whose size is zero is kept with an empty `fov` (mosaics-cutout gives it its default field of view). |
| `--dedup-radius` `DEDUP_RADIUS` | `10.0 arcsec` | — | Radius the production phase treats two rows as the same object at. A bare number is arcsec. Default: 10.0 arcsec. |
| `--split-seed` `SPLIT_SEED` | `20260902` | — | Seed the split. It orders each stratum by hash(row_id, seed) and sets the two lattice phases that dither the tier boundaries and the label interleave, so every split column is a pure function of the row and this number -- reproducible across machines and thread counts. Change it only to draw a genuinely independent split of the same data. Default: 20260902. |
| `--split-sizes` `COLUMN=SIZE` | `['phot_split_1pm=0.001', 'phot_split_1pc=0.01', 'phot_split_10pc=0.1', 'phot_split=1.0']` | — | The nested tiers, smallest first, as column=size. A size at or below 1 is a share of the catalogue; anything above 1 is an absolute row count, which is the honest option for a catalogue small enough that one per mille is a smoke test. The subsets nest and a row keeps the same train/val/test label in every tier it belongs to, so scaling up adds data instead of swapping it. Default: phot_split_1pm=0.001 phot_split_1pc=0.01 phot_split_10pc=0.1 phot_split=1.0. |
| `--split-ratios` `LABEL=PPM` | `['f=800000', 'v=100000', 't=100000']` | — | Train/validation/test labels and their shares in parts per million, which must sum to 1000000. Default: f=800000 v=100000 t=100000. |
| `--split-bins` `SPLIT_BINS` | `20` | — | Quantile bins per continuous stratifier. Rows with no finite value get a bin of their own on top of these. Default: 20. |
| `--split-stratifiers` `COLUMN` | `['ls11_mag_r', 'z']` | — | Continuous columns whose joint distribution every tier preserves. Default: ls11_mag_r z. |
| `--split-categoricals` `COLUMN` | `['has_spec']` | — | Boolean columns that are a further axis of the same stratum grid. In the grid rather than constrained afterwards: two sequential constraints fight, one joint grid satisfies both. Default: has_spec. |
| `--precedence` `COLUMN:ORDER` | `['has_spec:desc', 'ls11_mag_r:asc', 'ls11_mag_r_err:asc']` | — | Which row survives a duplicate group, most important criterion first, as column:asc or column:desc. Nulls always sort last, so a row missing the criterion never beats one that has it. Default: has_spec:desc ls11_mag_r:asc ls11_mag_r_err:asc. |
| `--proxy` `PROXY` | `None` | — | Proxy URL, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8888 to route through a mosaics proxy pool. HTTPS_PROXY is honoured when this is omitted. |
| `--max-per-origin` `MAX_PER_ORIGIN` | `3` | — | In-flight requests per host per source IP, which is what an archive actually throttles on. Behind a proxy pool the real ceiling is this times the number of connected workers, read from --proxy-stats-url. Default: 3. |
| `--retries` `RETRIES` | `5` | — | Attempts per request. Only transient failures consume attempts; a 404 fails immediately. Default: 5. |
| `--timeout` `TIMEOUT` | `60.0` | — | Per-request timeout in seconds. Default: 60.0. |
| `--proxy-stats-url` `URL` | `None` | — | URL of a mosaics proxy stats endpoint, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8889/stats. Read once at startup to learn how many workers are connected, which is what turns --max-per-origin into the real per-host ceiling, and polled per batch for the telemetry panel when --wandb is on. A proxy that cannot be reached is treated as a single source IP. |
| `--wandb` | `false` | — | Publish step states, timings, the targets report and the catalogue summary to Weights & Biases. Best-effort: a W&B outage never aborts or slows the run, and with this off no wandb import is attempted at all. |
| `--wandb-project` `WANDB_PROJECT` | `None` | — | W&B project. Default: whatever WANDB_PROJECT says. |

| `--workers`, `-j` `WORKERS` | `4` | — | Batches or chunks in flight inside one step. Several steps run at once as well (see --steps-per-source), so the requests in flight against one archive are the product of the two. Default: 4. |
| `--steps-per-source` `STEPS_PER_SOURCE` | `2` | — | Steps talking to the same archive that may run at once. Steps on different archives never wait for each other, so a HATS crossmatch runs beside an Astro Data Lab one. Each step fans out by --workers itself, so the requests in flight against one archive are the product of the two. Default: 2. |

Each step up quarters a cell: order 4 is 3072 cells of 13.4 deg2, order 5 is 12288 of 3.36 deg2, order 6 is 49152 of 0.84 deg2. A cell is one query, one ledger entry and one unit of resume, so a coarser order means fewer, larger requests and a crash costs more. It is part of every store fingerprint -- cells of two orders are not the same work units -- so changing it refetches everything. | `--duckdb-memory` `DUCKDB_MEMORY` | `None` | — | Memory the candidate join and the production phase may give DuckDB, in DuckDB's spelling: 64GB, 512MiB. | `--log-level` `LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL` | Logging verbosity, for every module at once. DEBUG adds the full text of each generated query. Default: INFO. |
| `--status-interval` `STATUS_INTERVAL` | `30.0` | — | Seconds between [PIPELINE STATUS] blocks, which say how many of the roughly thirty steps are done and which are in flight. A step can be silent for minutes, so this is what tells a quiet run from a stuck one. 0 turns them off. Default: 30. |

# Input Table Formats & Coordinate Conventions

Every MOSAICS command that takes a target list (`-t` / `--targets` on `mosaics-cutout`, `mosaics-spectrum`, `mosaics-crossmatch run` (as `-i` / `--input`), `mosaics-query ssa`, and `-i` / `--input` on `mosaics-hipscat`) reads it through a unified table reader.

## 1. Supported file formats

Format is detected automatically from the file or directory extension:

| Extension | Format | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.parquet`, `.pq` | Apache Parquet | Recommended for large tables ($N \ge 10^5$); preserves Arrow types and metadata. |
| `.lance` | Lance dataset | Directory format produced by `mosaics-cutout`, `mosaics-spectrum`, and `mosaics-targets`. |
| `.fits`, `.fit`, `.fts` | FITS binary or ASCII table | Reads the first table HDU; blank ASCII integer fields are preserved as nulls rather than `0`. |
| `.csv`, `.tsv` | Delimited text | Comma- or tab-separated UTF-8 text with a header row. |
| `.feather`, `.arrow`, `.ipc` | Arrow IPC / Feather | Memory-mapped columnar format. |

All input columns are preserved in the output dataset along with any new image, spectrum, or crossmatch columns.

## 2. Required columns and automatic inference

Target-based pipelines require three logical columns:

| Logical role | CLI override flag | Auto-detected column names (case-insensitive) | Units / Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Unique key** | `--id-col` | `id`, `targetid`, `objid`, `source_id`, `ls_id_dr11`, `mosaics_id` (generated as 0-based `mosaics_id` when omitted and no `id` column is present) | Integer or string; **must be unique** across all rows. |
| **Right ascension** | `--ra-col` | `ra`, `coord_ra`, `raj2000`, `plug_ra`, `mean_fiber_ra`, `ra_icrs` | ICRS decimal degrees $[0, 360)$. |
| **Declination** | `--dec-col` | `dec`, `coord_dec`, `dej2000`, `plug_dec`, `mean_fiber_dec`, `dec_icrs` | ICRS decimal degrees $[-90, +90]$. |

## 3. Optional per-target field of view (`--fov-col`)

By default, `mosaics-cutout` uses a constant angular field of view (`--fov` and `--fov-unit`, default `0.5 arcmin`) for every stamp. When extracting cutouts from a `mosaics-targets` production catalogue (which computes an object-adaptive `fov` column in arcseconds), pass `--fov-col fov --fov-unit arcsec` so each stamp's angular width scales with the galaxy's size while keeping the output pixel grid (`--size`, e.g. `96x96`) fixed. `mosaics-fov` and `mosaics-crossmatch run --fov` make the same column for any table, and [Field of view](../concepts/field-of-view.md) explains how it is computed.

## 4. Sample target files

The repository ships sample target tables under `test/` for dry runs and testing:

- `test/objects_sample_1k.csv`: 1,000 extragalactic sky positions with `id`, `ra`, `dec`, and survey identifiers.


# Crossmatch Output Schema

`mosaics-crossmatch run` joins a table of positions against one or more surveys. What it writes is the joined table, a run account, a report and, when a task failed, a failures file. Every file is named after the output's stem, so two runs in one folder do not overwrite each other.

## 1. The joined table (`-o` / `--output`)

Only `(key, ra, dec)` is sent to an archive. When the tasks finish, each survey's columns are joined back onto the **whole input table** in memory and the result is written to `--output` (Parquet, FITS, VOTable, CSV, ...):

1. **Every input column**, in its original order and type. Input rows keep their place: a row that was not matched, had no usable position, or whose task failed is still there.
2. **For each survey, in the order they were matched**, the columns its definition names, then two the run adds:
   - `<prefix>_<alias>` for each column of the survey's `column_mapping` (or `--columns`), where the prefix is the survey's own (`wise_`, `lsstdp2_`, `euclidq1p_`), `--prefix`'s, or none (`--no-prefix`, and an ad hoc source given no prefix).
   - `<prefix>_dist_arcsec`: the great-circle separation to the counterpart, in arcseconds (`dist_arcsec` with no prefix).
   - `<prefix>_nmatch`: how many counterparts lay inside the radius before the nearest was kept (`nmatch` with no prefix).
3. **Join semantics (`--join`):**
   - `left` (default): keeps every input row, with a survey's columns empty where it found nothing.
   - `inner`: keeps the rows matched in every survey.
4. **Multiplicity (`--all-matches`, one survey only):** by default the nearest counterpart is kept per input row (ties broken by the counterpart's position, so the answer does not depend on the order responses arrived in); with `--all-matches` every pair inside the radius is kept, one output row per pair.

5. **Field of view (`--fov SURVEY`):** one more column at the end, `fov` (`float32`, arcseconds): the edge of the square cutout that frames the galaxy, computed from that survey's shape and `r` magnitude columns (see [`mosaics-fov`](../cli/fov.md)). It is empty where the survey found no counterpart, where the counterpart has neither a usable ellipticity nor a half-light radius, and where its size comes out as zero; the row is kept. With `--hle` the value is the half-light-ellipse method's alone, and a counterpart with a radius but no ellipticity gets none. A FITS or VOTable output carries its unit. See [Field of view](../concepts/field-of-view.md).

Two surveys, or a survey and the input, may not claim the same output name: that is refused before any request is sent. Integer columns that gain empty values are written as nullable integers, so a 19-digit identifier is never rounded through a float. A FITS or VOTable output carries each remote column's unit, content label and description as the archive wrote them.

## 2. The run account (`<output-stem>.crossmatch.yaml`)

The complete machine-readable summary of the run, and the only thing the report reads:

| Key | Content |
|---|---|
| `schema` | `mosaics-crossmatch/1` |
| `config` | the job and survey files in play, every argument with where its value came from (default, flag or a file), the definitions after the overrides, the flags in force, and which environment variable each credential came from (never its value) |
| `input` | rows, columns, the position columns used, and the rows without a usable position |
| `surveys.<label>` | per survey: adapter and strategy, service and table, prefix, the radius with its origin (library, override or flag) and the note it rests on, the columns requested and returned with the archive's description of each, tasks planned/done/cached/failed, rows uploaded/matched/failed, pairs, the separation tally, the multiplicity tally, the footprint filter's counts and sky maps, errors, time, requests and the rate limiter |
| `fov` | only with `--fov`: the survey it came from, the column added, the columns it read, the `method` (`ellipse-or-circle` or `half-light-ellipse`), and how many rows took each form: `ellipse`, `circle`, `half-light ellipse` and `none` |
| `counts`, `output`, `failures` | rows in and out, the columns added, the failed tasks in total |
| `tables` | a column profile and sky map of the input and of the output |
| `http`, `timing`, `provenance` | requests per service, wall clock, and the software version, revision and host |

## 3. The report (`<output-stem>.report/`)

- `crossmatch.scireport.zip`: sealed `scireport` bundle built with template `mosaics-crossmatch@1`.
- `md/`: chapter-split Markdown (`index.md`, `summary.md`, `overview.md`, `input.md`, one `survey-<label>.md` per survey, `output.md`, `network.md`, `conclusion.md`, `appendix.md`).
- `pdf/report.pdf`: rendered PDF report (unless `--no-report-pdf` was passed).

## 4. The failures file (`<output-stem>.failures.parquet`)

Written whenever a task still failed after its retries. One row per failed task: `survey`, `task`, `rows` (how many input rows it owned), `keys` (their row positions in the input, from 0) and `error`. Running the same command again repeats only the failed tasks, because finished ones are cached under `.mosaics-crossmatch/<output-stem>/` beside the output.


# Cutout Lance Dataset Schema

`mosaics-cutout` writes a directory `<output>.lance` in [Lance](https://lancedb.github.io/lance/) format (built on Apache Arrow), plus an optional `<output>.failures.parquet` sidecar when one or more stamps fail.

## 1. Column layout

Every row in `<output>.lance` contains:

1. **All columns from the input target table** (plus `mosaics_id: int64` if no key column was supplied).
2. **One fixed-shape tensor column per cutout service / band:**
   - **Single-band cutouts (`cutout full`, `lsv`, `nersc`, `sia`, `vsa`, single-band `hips`):** named `cutout_<survey>_<band>` (or `image` for single-service runs such as `mosaics-cutout hips`), stored as an Arrow `FixedShapeTensorType` of element type `float32` (or `uint8` for JPEG/PNG) and logical shape `(C, H, W)` where `C = 1` for a single band, `C = N` for an unsplit multi-band stack, or `C = 3` for `[color]` RGB stamps, and `H = W = --size`.
   - **Failed stamps:** represented as an Arrow `null` at the row level (never an array of `NaN`s or zeros), so `is_null()` distinguishes a failed cutout from a dark sky region.

## 2. Arrow field calibration metadata

Each cutout tensor field in the Lance schema carries its photometric pixel calibration in Arrow field metadata (`field.metadata`, UTF-8 byte keys and values):

| Metadata key | Example value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mosaics_unit` | `b"nanomaggy"`, `b"ab_zeropoint"`, `b"counts_per_s"`, `b"unknown"` | Physical calibration regime of the pixel values. |
| `mosaics_calibration` | `b"calibrated"` or `b"uncalibrated"` | Whether the pixels can be converted directly to physical flux density ($\mu\text{Jy}$). |
| `mosaics_scale` | `b"3.6307805"` | Multiplicative factor converting native pixel values to microjanskys ($\mu\text{Jy}$), where $3.6307805\ \mu\text{Jy} = 1\ \text{nanomaggy}$ ($m_{\text{AB}} = 22.5$). |
| `mosaics_offset` | `b"0.0"` | Additive offset in microjanskys applied after scaling ($\text{flux}_{\mu\text{Jy}} = \text{pixel} \times \text{scale} + \text{offset}$). |

## 3. The `.failures.parquet` sidecar

When any `(target, service)` request fails during a run, MOSAICS writes `<output>.failures.parquet` next to `<output>.lance`:

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<id_col>` | matches input key | Target key value from the input table. |
| `service` | `string` | Service label (`<survey>:<adapter>:<band_or_stack>`, e.g. `ls11:lsv:stack`). |
| `category` | `string` | Failure classification (`http_status`, `timeout`, `decode`, `empty_coverage`, `network`). |
| `status` | `int32` (nullable) | HTTP status code when applicable (`404`, `429`, `503`, ...). |
| `error` | `string` | Human-readable error message from the transport or decoder. |
| `url` | `string` (nullable) | Request URL that failed. |


# Reading Output Datasets in Python

MOSAICS writes standard Apache Parquet (`.parquet`) and Lance (`.lance`) datasets that open directly in `lance` (`pylance`), `pyarrow`, `pandas`, and PyTorch without requiring MOSAICS itself to be imported.

## 1. Reading a cutout or spectrum Lance dataset with `lance` and `pyarrow`

```python
import lance
import numpy as np

# Open the dataset on disk (zero-copy metadata read)
ds = lance.dataset('cutouts.lance')
print(ds.schema)

# Inspect pixel calibration metadata on a cutout column
field = ds.schema.field('cutout_ls11_g')
print(field.metadata)
# {b'mosaics_unit': b'nanomaggy', b'mosaics_calibration': b'calibrated', b'mosaics_scale': b'3.6307805', b'mosaics_offset': b'0.0'}

# Read a slice of rows or specific columns into PyArrow
table = ds.to_table(columns=['id', 'ra', 'dec', 'cutout_ls11_g'], limit=32)

# Convert a FixedShapeTensor column to a (N, C, H, W) NumPy float32 array
tensor_col = table['cutout_ls11_g'].combine_chunks()
stamps = tensor_col.to_numpy_ndarray()  # shape: (32, 1, 96, 96)
```

## 2. Reading variable-length spectra and applying the boolean mask

```python
import lance
import numpy as np

ds = lance.dataset('sdss17_spectra.lance')
table = ds.to_table(
  columns=['id', 'sdss17_wavelength', 'sdss17_flux', 'sdss17_error', 'sdss17_mask'],
  limit=10,
)

for row_idx in range(table.num_rows):
  if table['sdss17_flux'][row_idx].is_valid:
    wl = np.asarray(table['sdss17_wavelength'][row_idx].as_py(), dtype=np.float32)
    flux = np.asarray(table['sdss17_flux'][row_idx].as_py(), dtype=np.float32)
    err = np.asarray(table['sdss17_error'][row_idx].as_py(), dtype=np.float32)
    usable = np.asarray(table['sdss17_mask'][row_idx].as_py(), dtype=bool)
    # Keep only unmasked samples (usable == True)
    wl_clean, flux_clean, err_clean = wl[usable], flux[usable], err[usable]
```

## 3. Reading the targets catalogue with `pyarrow` or `pandas`

```python
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

# Read only the anchor coordinates, redshift, and Legacy Survey + VHS magnitudes
cols = [
  'id', 'ra', 'dec', 'z', 'z_survey', 'split',
  'ls11', 'ls11_mag_g', 'ls11_mag_r', 'ls11_mag_z',
  'vhs5', 'vhs5_mag_aper3_j', 'vhs5_mag_aper3_ks',
]
df = pd.read_parquet('targets_run/targets.parquet', columns=cols)
train_df = df[df['split'] == 'train']
```

## 4. Inspecting the `.failures.parquet` sidecar

```python
import pandas as pd

failures = pd.read_parquet('cutouts.failures.parquet')
print(failures.groupby(['service', 'category']).size())
```


# Spectrum Lance Dataset Schema

`mosaics-spectrum` writes a Lance dataset `<output>.lance` containing all input target columns alongside variable-length Arrow `large_list` columns for each spectroscopic survey.

## 1. Parallel `large_list` columns

For each spectroscopic survey `<slug>` (`sdss17`, `desi1`, `lamost11`, `6dfgs`, `2dfgrs`, `hasp`, `euclidq1`), the dataset contains the parallel arrays declared in `defs/surveys/<slug>.yaml` under `spectra[].arrays`:

| Column | Arrow Type | Units | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{slug}_flux` | `large_list<item: float32>` | $10^{-17}\ \text{erg}\ \text{s}^{-1}\ \text{cm}^{-2}\ \text{\AA}^{-1}$ (when calibrated) or native counts | 1D spectral flux density per wavelength pixel. |
| `{slug}_error` | `large_list<item: float32>` | Same unit as `{slug}_flux` | $1\sigma$ uncertainty per pixel (omitted for `2dfgrs` and `6dfgs`, which publish no per-pixel error). |
| `{slug}_wavelength` | `large_list<item: float32>` | Angstrom ($\text{\AA}$) | Observer-frame wavelength per pixel. |
| `{slug}_mask` | `large_list<item: bool>` | Boolean (`true` = usable) | Per-pixel usability flag combining finiteness, archive quality bitmasks, positive error, and `--snr-floor`. |

On every row for a given `<slug>`, all present array columns have **identical list length** ($L \ge 0$), or all are simultaneously Arrow `null` when the observation failed or was not available.

## 2. Field and schema metadata

Each `{slug}_flux` field carries calibration metadata in its Arrow field metadata (`field.metadata`):

| Metadata key | Example value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mosaics_unit` | `b"1e-17 erg / (Angstrom cm2 s)"` or `b"counts"` | Flux unit after applying `spectroscopic_system.flux_scale`. |
| `mosaics_calibration` | `b"absolute"`, `b"relative"`, `b"none"`, `b"unknown"` | Spectroscopic flux calibration regime from `spectroscopic_system.flux_calibration`. |
| `mosaics_scale` | `b"1.0"` | Multiplier applied during decoding. |
| `mosaics_snr_floor` | `b"2.0"` | Minimum per-pixel signal-to-noise ratio applied when computing `{slug}_mask` (when `--snr-floor` was set). |


# Targets Production Catalogue Schema

`mosaics-targets` writes the final crossmatched, homogenised catalogue to `<output>/targets.parquet` (or `.lance`), stamped with schema version metadata key `mosaics_catalog_schema`.

## 1. Core anchor and summary columns

Every row represents one unique astronomical source anchored on the resolved Legacy Survey DR11 primary catalogue (`ls11`) and/or spectroscopic selections:

| Column | Type | Units | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `int64` | — | Canonical target identifier (`ls11_id` when matched to DR11, or deterministic hash for unrescued spectroscopic-only sources). |
| `ra` | `float64` | `deg` | Best available right ascension (ICRS). |
| `dec` | `float64` | `deg` | Best available declination (ICRS). |
| `z` | `float32` | — | Best spectroscopic redshift, selected across all matching spectroscopic surveys in order of `spectroscopic_system.redshift_rank`. |
| `z_err` | `float32` | — | $1\sigma$ uncertainty on `z`. |
| `z_survey` | `string` | — | Survey slug that contributed `z` (`desi1`, `sdss17`, `lamost11`, `6dfgs`, `2dfgrs`, `euclidq1s`, `hasp`). |
| `fov` | `float32` | `arcsec` | Recommended square cutout edge length in arcseconds, from the Legacy Survey shape and `r` magnitude of the target (ellipse form, circle form where the ellipse is missing, or the half-light ellipse alone with `--hle`). A row with a missing shape or magnitude measurement is not in the catalogue; a row whose size is zero is, with an empty (null) `fov`, and `mosaics-cutout` gives it a default field of view (`--default-fov`, or the median of the valid values). See [Field of view](../concepts/field-of-view.md); `mosaics-cutout` needs `--fov-unit arcsec` to read it. |
| `split` | `string` | — | Spatial HEALPix split assignment (`train`, `val`, `test`) preventing neighbour leakage across splits. |

## 2. Per-survey detection flags

For every photometric and spectroscopic survey prefix `<prefix>` (`ls11`, `gaia3`, `unwise`, `denis3`, `euclidq1p`, `euclidq1s`, `galex`, `hsc3`, `hst2`, `kids3`, `sdss16`, `skymapper4`, `twomass`, `ukidss9`, `ukidss11`, `vhs5`, `wise`, `2dfgrs`, `6dfgs`, `desi1`, `hasp`, `lamost11`, `sdss17`), a boolean column `<prefix>` (`bool`, non-nullable) indicates whether the target has valid measurements from that survey after applying post-hoc `catalog_filters`.

## 3. Homogenised photometric columns

Every photometric measurement block declared under `photometric_system.measurements` (and `provides.<prefix>.measurements`) is homogenised onto a uniform physical scale:

- **AB magnitudes:** `<prefix>_mag_<aperture>_<band>` and `<prefix>_mag_err_<aperture>_<band>` (or `<prefix>_mag_<band>` when `aperture` is `default`), in AB magnitudes (`float32`). Native Vega magnitudes (`vega_mag`) are shifted by `+vega_offsets[band]`, and Lupton `asinh_mag` columns are converted to linear flux and AB magnitudes.
- **Linear fluxes:** `<prefix>_flux_<aperture>_<band>` and `<prefix>_flux_err_<aperture>_<band>`, converted to **microjanskys ($\mu\text{Jy}$)** (`float32`), where $1\ \text{nanomaggy} = 3.6307805\ \mu\text{Jy}$ and $m_{\text{AB}} = 23.90 - 2.5 \log_{10}(f_{\mu\text{Jy}})$. Native inverse variances (`error_kind: ivar`) are converted to $1\sigma$ flux uncertainties in $\mu\text{Jy}$.

## 4. Spectroscopic survey columns

Each spectroscopic survey prefix `<spec_prefix>` (`desi1`, `sdss17`, `lamost11`, `6dfgs`, `2dfgrs`, `hasp`, `euclidq1s`) contributes its own prefixed columns:

- `<spec_prefix>_id`, `<spec_prefix>_ra`, `<spec_prefix>_dec`
- `<spec_prefix>_z`, `<spec_prefix>_z_err`
- Survey-specific fibre/instrument metadata (`sdss17_plate`, `sdss17_mjd`, `sdss17_fiberid`, `lamost11_obsid`, `sixdfgs_access_url`, `hst_access_url`, `euclid_access_url`) required downstream by `mosaics-spectrum`.


# Survey Configuration Reference

Every survey in `mosaics` is defined once in a declarative YAML file under `defs/surveys/<slug>.yaml`. Entrypoint files under `defs/*.yaml` list the surveys a run covers (`surveys:`), change some of them (`overrides:`) and are passed to CLI commands via `--config`.

This page documents every root section, every section key, and every adapter parameter accepted by the configuration loader, followed by complete worked examples that pass strict loader validation.

## File Structure & Composition

There are two kinds of YAML file, and a file is one or the other:

- A **survey file** defines one survey. The files in `defs/surveys/` are the *library*: read-only for users, who extend them rather than edit them.
- An **entrypoint** maps the arguments of one command and says which survey files it runs on. `defs/*.yaml` are the shipped entrypoints.

A **survey file** (`defs/surveys/<slug>.yaml`) declares `survey_slug`, `name`, and whichever of the ten capability and metadata sections apply to that survey (`catalog`, `catalog_filters`, `cutout`, `spectra`, `photometric_system`, `spectroscopic_system`, `target_selection`, `provides`, `column_mapping`, `crossmatch`). It is unfolded: keys at the top, no `<slug>:` wrapper.

An **entrypoint** declares `surveys:` (the roster: a string or list of survey files or glob patterns), an optional `exclude:` (files to leave out of the roster), an optional `overrides:` mapping of changes to roster surveys, and an optional `extends:` of other entrypoints:

```yaml
surveys:
  - surveys/sdss20
  - surveys/ps1
  - surveys/viking

exclude:
  - surveys/viking

overrides:
  surveys/ps1:
    cutout: []
```

`overrides:` keys are globs over a roster survey's name (its path under `defs/`, without `.yaml`, e.g. `surveys/ps1`) or its slug (`ps1`). Every key that matches a survey is merged over it, deeply, before validation; the less specific key goes first, so the specific key wins a conflict and the general one still supplies what it leaves unset. A key that matches no roster survey logs a warning.

On the command line, `--survey REF …` replaces the entrypoint's roster (the entrypoint's `overrides:` still apply), `--exclude-survey REF …` adds to `exclude:`, and every run logs the **effective configuration**: the files in play, the arguments with where each value came from, and for each survey every key an override changed, as `library value -> effective value`. The complete definitions are logged at `debug`.

To change a library survey for good in your own runs, write a **survey file that extends it** and list that file instead of the library one:

```yaml
extends: surveys/ps1.yaml
name: Pan-STARRS1 DR1 (group copy)
cutout: []
```

When `extends:` is evaluated:
- It is a plain dictionary default: the extended file supplies defaults and the extending file overrides them. It never adds surveys to a run; that is `surveys:`.
- An entrypoint extends entrypoints and a survey file extends survey files. Crossing raises an error that shows the new spelling.
- Each entry expands `~` and environment variables. Absolute paths are used as given, and the `.yaml` suffix is optional everywhere (`surveys/ps1`).
- Relative paths are resolved against the naming file's directory, then `$CWD`, then `defs/`, deduplicated by resolved path. The first base with a match wins; if a relative path exists in multiple distinct bases, a warning is logged naming the winner and shadowed paths. `surveys:` and `exclude:` use the same lookup.
- Recursive extension is supported; circular references are detected and raise an error with the full chain.
- Maps are deep-merged left to right and the extending file wins; lists replace the inherited list, and `key: null` removes the key.
- An extension takes its slug from the merged result, so a roster that lists both an extension and the file it extends raises.
- The root `--config` option resolves relative paths against `$CWD`, then `defs/` (e.g. `--config targets.yaml` works from anywhere, and so does the repository-root spelling `--config defs/targets.yaml`).
- Validation is **strict**: any unknown root key, unknown section key, unknown `adapter_params` key for the declared `(section, adapter)` pair, invalid enum value, or unprefixed column alias raises an immediate validation error before any archive is contacted.

### Column Prefix Rule

A survey's output column prefix is derived automatically from its `survey_slug`:
- If a survey defines **either** a photometric catalog (`type: photometric`) **or** a spectroscopic catalog (`type: spectroscopic`), its columns take the bare slug prefix `{slug}_`.
- If a survey defines **both** a photometric and a spectroscopic catalog in the same file (for example, `euclidq1`), the photometric catalog uses `{slug}p_` and the spectroscopic catalog uses `{slug}s_` so their coordinate and identifier columns (`{prefix}ra`, `{prefix}dec`) never collide.

---

## Configuration Sections

<!-- generated:config-sections -->
### Entrypoint top-level keys (`defs/*.yaml`)

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `extends` | str or list of str | no | [] | relative or absolute paths, ~ or globs; .yaml optional | Files whose keys are the defaults of this one, merged left to right (later wins, this file last). An entrypoint extends entrypoints and a survey file extends survey files; relative paths search the naming file's directory, then $CWD, then defs/. |
| `surveys` | str or list of str | no | [] | survey files by relative or absolute path, ~ or globs; .yaml optional | The roster, the survey files a run covers, in declaration order (globs sorted, a file named twice counts once). `--survey` on the command line replaces it. |
| `exclude` | str or list of str | no | [] | relative or absolute paths, ~ or globs; .yaml optional | Files to remove from the roster; an entry matching no files is allowed and logged at info. `--exclude-survey` adds to it. |
| `overrides` | mapping (survey key -> partial survey definition) | no | {} | keys are globs over a survey file's name (`surveys/wise`) or slug (`wise`) | Partial survey definitions merged deeply over each roster survey the key matches, after its own `extends` chain and before validation; less specific keys apply first. Any other top-level key of an entrypoint is an argument of the command that reads it. |

### Survey definition root keys (`defs/surveys/<slug>.yaml`)

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `survey_slug` | str | yes | — | must equal the YAML file stem | Canonical lowercase identifier for the survey and default column prefix. |
| `name` | str | yes | — | non-empty string | Human-readable survey and data-release name used in logs, plans, and reports. |
| `catalog` | list of catalog entries | no | [] | at most one entry per `type` (`photometric`, `spectroscopic`) | Remote or local catalogues queried for target extraction or crossmatching. |
| `catalog_filters` | mapping (prefix -> SQL expression or note) | no | {} | `<prefix>` and `<prefix>_note` | Post-hoc DuckDB SQL quality/depth/redshift cuts applied during production (nulls failing survey columns without dropping the row). |
| `cutout` | list of cutout entries | no | [] | see Cutout entry keys | Image cutout backends (`hips`, `lsv`, `nersc`, `sia`, `vsa`) serving this survey's passbands. |
| `spectra` | list of spectra entries | no | [] | see Spectra entry keys | 1D spectrum download backends (`url`, `template`, `sparcl`, `desi-healpix`). |
| `photometric_system` | mapping | no | None | see Photometric system keys | Passband SVO filter identifiers, flux/magnitude homogenisation rules, and image pixel calibration. |
| `spectroscopic_system` | mapping | no | None | see Spectroscopic system keys | Spectrograph fibre diameter, disperser, redshift tiebreak rank, and flux calibration facts. |
| `target_selection` | mapping | no | None | see Target selection keys | How this survey seeds or joins the candidate table in the targets pipeline. |
| `provides` | mapping (prefix -> photometric system) | no | {} | see Provides keys | Another survey's photometry already carried inside this survey's extraction query (e.g. `gaia3` and `unwise` inside `ls11`). |
| `column_mapping` | mapping (remote_column -> alias) | no | {} | alias without prefix (an alias that starts with `<prefix>_` raises); glob keys with `{1}` captures; a mapping value names a `provides` prefix | Projection and column renaming applied when crossmatching against this survey's photometric catalogue. The loader adds the catalog's prefix to every alias, or the hosted survey's for the columns under its `provides` key. |
| `crossmatch` | mapping | no | None | see Crossmatch keys | How a table of positions is matched against this survey. Required for a survey with an `lsdb` catalog; `crossmatch` null removes it, and a survey without it takes no part in `mosaics-crossmatch`. |

### `catalog[]` entry keys

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | yes | — | `{slug}`, or `{slug}p` / `{slug}s` when both photometric and spectroscopic catalogues exist | Column prefix and catalogue identifier for this entry. |
| `type` | str | yes | — | `photometric`, `spectroscopic` | Whether this catalogue provides broadband photometry or spectroscopic redshifts/targets. |
| `adapter` | str | yes | — | `adl`, `tap`, `crossid`, `local`, `nersc`, `lsdb` | Catalogue query provider backend. |
| `adapter_params` | mapping | no | {} | see Adapter parameters by catalog adapter | Provider-specific connection, table, coordinate, and chunking settings. |
| `enabled` | bool | no | true | `true`, `false` | When `false`, the catalogue entry is skipped by all pipelines. |
| `unflagged` | str | no | None | free text explanation | Reason why the archive provides no usable quality flag for this catalogue's photometry. |

### `cutout[]` entry keys

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `adapter` | str | yes | — | `hips`, `lsv`, `nersc`, `sia`, `vsa` | Cutout retrieval backend. |
| `adapter_params` | mapping | no | {} | backend-specific parameters (`hips_id`, `hips_ids`, `layer`, `bands`, `service_url`, `fov`) | Backend-specific parameters passed to the cutout adapter. |
| `bands` | list of str | yes | — | lowercase band tokens (e.g. `[g, r, i, z]`) or `[color]` | Output band tokens determining the Lance dataset column names (`cutout_<slug>_<band>`). |
| `enabled` | bool | no | true | `true`, `false` | Whether `cutout full` considers this backend entry. |
| `pixel_unit` | str | no | None (inherits photometric_system.pixel_unit) | `nanomaggy`, `ab_zeropoint`, `counts_per_s`, `unknown` | Per-entry pixel calibration unit override. |
| `zeropoint` | float | no | None (inherits photometric_system.zeropoint) | finite float | Per-entry AB magnitude zero point override. |
| `pixel_unit_note` | str | no | None | free text | Provenance note explaining the per-entry pixel calibration. |
| `cost` | mapping | no | None | see Cutout cost keys | Optional cost-model overrides used when `cutout full` routes bands across multiple backends. |
| `label` | str | no | `<slug>:<adapter>:<band_or_stack>` | unique string within the run | Identifier recorded in the `.failures.parquet` sidecar for this cutout service. |

### `cutout[].cost` keys

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `latency_s` | float | no | adapter default | >= 0 | Estimated per-request HTTP latency in seconds. |
| `bandwidth_bps` | float | no | adapter default | > 0 | Estimated download throughput in bytes per second. |
| `concurrency` | int | no | adapter default | >= 1 | Effective concurrent requests allowed by the service. |
| `render_seconds` | float | no | adapter default | >= 0 | Server-side or local cutout rendering CPU time per target in seconds. |
| `bytes_penalty_s_per_gb` | float | no | adapter default | >= 0 | Disk/network amortisation penalty in seconds per gigabyte downloaded. |

### `spectra[]` entry keys

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `adapter` | str | yes | — | `url`, `template`, `sparcl`, `desi-healpix` | Spectrum retrieval backend. |
| `adapter_params` | mapping | no | {} | backend-specific parameters (`url_template`, `data_release`, `specprod`, `coadd_type`, `survey`, `program`) | Parameters forwarded to the spectrum adapter. |
| `format` | str | no | None | `sdss`, `lamost-mrs`, `2dfgrs`, `6dfgs`, `hasp`, `euclid-q1`, `sparcl`, `desi-healpix` | FITS/VOTable decoder name in `mosaics.spectrum.decode`. |
| `arrays` | list of str | no | [] | subset of `flux`, `error`, `wavelength`, `mask` | Parallel spectrum arrays published by this archive and written to the output Lance dataset. |
| `enabled` | bool | no | true | `true`, `false` | Whether this spectrum backend is active (two enabled backends may not fill the same column). |

### `photometric_system` keys

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `filters` | mapping (band -> SVO filter ID) | no | {} | lowercase band token -> `Facility/Instrument.Filter` | Maps each band token to its SVO Filter Profile Service identifier; its keys define the survey's band list. |
| `filter_variants` | mapping | no | None | see Filter variant keys | Per-row filter-profile override when a survey combines multiple instruments or hemispheres (e.g. `ls11_hemisphere`). |
| `vega_offsets` | mapping (band -> float) | no | {} | declared band tokens -> `m_AB - m_Vega` | Additive AB minus Vega zero-point offsets used to convert `vega_mag` columns to AB magnitudes and microjanskys. |
| `measurements` | list of measurement mappings | no | [] | see Photometric measurement keys | Native photometric measurement systems, apertures, and uncertainty encodings published by the catalogue. |
| `detection_column` | str | no | None | local column alias starting with `<prefix>_` | Column whose non-null presence marks a target as detected by this survey. |
| `pixel_unit` | str | no | `unknown` | `nanomaggy`, `ab_zeropoint`, `counts_per_s`, `unknown` | Physical or calibration unit of the survey's cutout image pixels. |
| `zeropoint` | float | no | None | finite float | Survey-wide AB magnitude zero point for cutout pixels when `pixel_unit` is `ab_zeropoint` or `counts_per_s`. |
| `pixel_unit_note` | str | no | None | free text | Provenance explanation and citation for the image pixel calibration. |
| `borrow_filters` | str | no | None | another survey's `survey_slug` | Borrows the passband `filters` dictionary from another survey definition (used by cutout-only releases such as `ls10` borrowing `ls11`). |

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `column` | str | yes | — | column name in the catalogue (e.g. `ls11_hemisphere`) | Catalogue column whose value selects which instrument filter mapping applies to a row. |
| `cases` | mapping (case_value -> mapping of band -> SVO filter ID) | yes | — | non-empty mapping covering declared bands | Maps each distinct value of `column` (such as `'N'` or `'S'`) to its per-band SVO filter identifiers. |

### `photometric_system.measurements[]` keys

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `system` | str | yes | — | `ab_mag`, `vega_mag`, `asinh_mag`, `linear` | Native photometric unit family of the raw catalogue columns before homogenisation to AB magnitudes and microjansky fluxes. |
| `bands` | list of str | no | all keys of `filters` | subset of declared band tokens | Bands covered by this measurement block. |
| `apertures` | list of str | no | `[default]` | aperture tokens (e.g. `default`, `aper3`, `petro`, `psf`, `cmodel`, `kron`) | Photometric aperture or model suffixes present in the column aliases (`<prefix>_<kind>_<aperture>_<band>`). |
| `scale` | float or mapping (band -> float) | no | 1.0 | positive float(s) | Multiplicative factor converting native linear flux units into microjanskys (`uJy`), required when `system: linear`. |
| `error_kind` | str | no | `linear` | `linear`, `ivar` | Whether native linear flux uncertainties are 1-sigma errors (`linear`) or inverse variances (`ivar`). |
| `errors` | bool | no | true | `true`, `false` | Set to `false` when the catalogue publishes no uncertainty column for this measurement block. |
| `offsets` | mapping (band -> float) | no | {} | declared band tokens -> float | Per-band additive residual offsets onto the AB magnitude scale. |
| `softening` | mapping (band -> float) | no | {} | declared band tokens -> positive float `b` | Lupton asinh softening parameters `b` per band, required when `system: asinh_mag`. |

### `spectroscopic_system` keys

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fiber_diameter` | float or str | no | None | positive float (arcseconds), `'per_row'`, or `None` | Entrance fibre or slit width in arcseconds, or `'per_row'` when selected as a column by the SQL query. |
| `disperser` | str | no | None | `grating`, `grism`, `prism`, `echelle`, `mixed` | Spectrograph dispersing element type. |
| `redshift_rank` | int | no | None | positive integer (smaller wins) | Priority rank when multiple spectroscopic surveys provide a redshift for the same target; `None` excludes the survey from tiebreaking. |
| `velocity_columns` | list of 2 str | no | None | `[velocity_col, velocity_err_col]` | Heliocentric recession velocity and uncertainty columns (in km/s) converted to redshift `z = v / c`. |
| `null_sentinel` | float | no | None | finite float (e.g. `-9999.0`) | Archive sentinel value replaced with `NULL` before redshift/velocity conversion. |
| `flux_scale` | float | no | None | positive float | Multiplier converting native spectrum flux values to `10^-17 erg s^-1 cm^-2 Angstrom^-1`. |
| `flux_calibration` | str | no | `unknown` | `absolute`, `relative`, `none`, `unknown` | Whether published 1D spectra are flux-calibrated in physical units (`absolute`), relative throughput (`relative`), or uncalibrated counts (`none`). |

### `target_selection` keys

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |

| `rescue_where` | str | no | None | SQL boolean expression (photometric selections only) | Relaxed SQL filter used during the photometric rescue stage for spectroscopic targets missed by the primary photometric selection. |
| `columns` | mapping (remote_column -> local_alias) | no | {} | `lsdb` adapter only; must include `<prefix>_id`, `<prefix>_ra`, `<prefix>_dec` | Column projection and alias map for HATS/LSDB target extraction (used instead of a SQL `query`). |
| `filters` | list of `[column, operator, value]` | no | [] | `lsdb` adapter only; operators `==`, `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `in`, `not in` | Parquet pushdown row filters applied during HATS/LSDB target extraction. |

### Crossmatch keys (`crossmatch:`)

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | angle | yes | — | a number (arcseconds) or a string such as `1.5 arcsec`; above 0 and at most 60 arcsec | The survey's match radius, the largest separation at which a catalogue object counts as a counterpart. It is a property of the survey's depth and astrometry, so it lives here and not in an adapter's transport knobs. |
| `radius_note` | str | no | None | non-empty string | What the radius rests on (the instrument facts and where they were read). A test requires it of every file shipped under `defs/surveys/`; a user's own file may omit it. |
| `catalog` | str | no | the enabled photometric catalog, else the enabled spectroscopic one | the `name` of an enabled `catalog` entry of this survey | Which catalog the radius and the strategy apply to. |
| `moc` | path | no | None | a MOC FITS file; a relative path is relative to the file that names it | The survey's footprint, for `--filter-moc`. Build it with `mosaics-crossmatch moc`; its existence is checked when a run uses it, not when the file loads. |
| `strategy` | str | no | `upload` | `upload`, `extract` (refused for `crossid` and `lsdb`) | `upload` sends the positions to the archive; `extract` fetches the survey's rows for the sky the input occupies and matches them here. |

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | str | yes | — | HTTP/HTTPS URL to a FITS or Parquet table | Archive URL of the bulk catalogue file downloaded once and converted to a local DuckDB/Parquet store. |
| `table` | str | yes | — | lowercase SQL identifier `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*` | Local table name under which SQL queries reference the converted catalogue file. |

## Adapter Parameters (`adapter_params`)

Each `catalog`, `cutout`, and `spectra` entry accepts an `adapter_params` mapping whose allowed keys depend on the chosen `adapter`.

<!-- generated:config-adapters -->
### `adl` (NSF NOIRLab Astro Data Lab TAP)

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `table` | str | yes | — | Fully qualified TAP table name on Astro Data Lab (e.g. `gaia_dr3.gaia_source`, `allwise.source`). |
| `mode` | str | no | `spatial` | Crossmatch join mode (`spatial` cone join or `relational` key join). |
| `key_column` | str | no | None | Local candidate column holding the pre-matched foreign key when `mode: relational`. |
| `remote_key_column` | str | no | None | Remote table primary key column matched against `key_column` when `mode: relational`. |
| `remote_ra_column` | str | no | `ra` | Right ascension column in the remote table used for spatial cone joins. |
| `remote_dec_column` | str | no | `dec` | Declination column in the remote table used for spatial cone joins. |
| `chunk_size` | int | no | 50000 | Number of target positions uploaded per TAP crossmatch batch. |
| `use_async` | bool | no | false | Submit queries as asynchronous UWS TAP jobs instead of synchronous requests. |
| `dialect` | str | no | `top` | Row-limiting SQL syntax (`top` for ADQL `SELECT TOP n`, `limit` for PostgreSQL `LIMIT n`). |

| `remote_key_column` | str | no | None | Remote key column when `mode: relational`. |

### `tap` (Generic IVOA TAP service)

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `use_async` | bool | no | false | Submit queries as asynchronous UWS TAP jobs. |

### `adl-healpix` (NSF NOIRLab Astro Data Lab public TAP, matched by `nest4096` ranges)

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `table` | str | yes | — | Fully qualified table on Astro Data Lab that carries a HEALPix NESTED index column (e.g. `gaia_dr3.gaia_source`, `allwise.source`, `ls_dr11.tractor`). |
| `service` | str | no | `datalab` (the public TAP at `https://datalab.noirlab.edu/tap`, no login) | A full TAP endpoint or a shorthand of the TAP services, for a test archive. |

| `remote_dec_column` | str | no | found by UCD (`pos.eq.dec`), then by name | Remote declination column name. |
| `index_column` | str | no | `nest4096` | The table's HEALPix NESTED index. Its values are checked against the returned positions on the first query of every run. |
| `index_order` | int | no | 12 (the order of `nest4096`) | The HEALPix order of `index_column`. |
| `max_rows_per_query` | int | no | 50000 | Most rows one query may return. A query whose result reaches it is split and asked again, never truncated. |
| `max_ranges_per_query` | int | no | 50 | Most index ranges one query may carry. The public TAP times out well above this (probed at 100 and 500). |
| `rows_per_deg2` | float | no | None (counted by a few `COUNT(*)` queries) | The table's mean source density per square degree. When given, the planner sends no counting query. |
