# UKIDSS DR11 (`ukidss11`)

<!-- generated:survey-page -->
The UKIRT Infrared Deep Sky Survey (UKIDSS) Data Release 11plus (DR11plus) Large Area Survey (LAS) is a wide-field near-infrared photometric survey covering approximately 4,000 deg² of the northern and equatorial sky in the $Y, J, H, K$ passbands. Observations were conducted using the Wide Field Camera (WFCAM) on the 3.8-metre United Kingdom Infrared Telescope (UKIRT) on Maunakea, reaching 5-sigma point-source depths of $Y = 20.2$, $J = 19.6$, $H = 18.8$, and $K = 18.2$ mag (Vega).

In `mosaics`, `ukidss11` provides near-infrared photometric catalogue crossmatching via Astro Data Lab TAP (`ukidss_dr11plus.lassource`). Extracted measurements include aperture-corrected 2.0 arcsec point-source magnitudes (`aper3`), Petrosian magnitudes (`petro`), and total Hall magnitudes (`hall`) along with photometric errors, morphological classification statistics, duplicate seam flags, and galactic extinction estimates. The survey definition also declares an IVOA Simple Image Access (SIA) cutout adapter for UKIDSS DR11 imaging from WFAU Edinburgh, which is disabled by default in shipped configurations.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| What MOSAICS extracts | Catalogue: `ukidss11` (photometric, `adl-healpix`); Cutouts: `sia` (y,j,h,k) |
| Archives | SIA (`wfaudata.roe.ac.uk`), `datalab.noirlab.edu` |
| Bands / wavelength range | `y` (`UKIRT/UKIDSS.Y`), `j` (`UKIRT/UKIDSS.J`), `h` (`UKIRT/UKIDSS.H`), `k` (`UKIRT/UKIDSS.K`) |
| Used by | `mosaics-targets` (crossmatch), `mosaics-cutout full`, `mosaics-crossmatch` |
| Crossmatch radius | `1` arcsec. DR1 median seeing 0.82 arcsec; astrometric rms 50-100 mas tied to 2MASS (Lawrence et al. 2007, arXiv:astro-ph/0604426, Table 2). These are DR1 values; no DR11 document was opened. Value set by the author (HG2, 2026-10-19); the instrument-based proposal was 0.5 arcsec. |

## Configuration

### The shipped file

Source: `defs/surveys/ukidss11.yaml`

```yaml
# UKIDSS DR11 -- photometry and cutouts.

survey_slug: ukidss11
name: UKIDSS DR11

catalog:
  - name: ukidss11
    type: photometric
    # Astro Data Lab's public TAP, by ranges of the table's `nest4096` index: no login, no
    # upload; the rows that come back are a superset of the matches and the match itself is
    # made here by haversine separation (HG3, 2026-10-20: Data Lab accounts can no longer be
    # authenticated, so the `adl` upload route is unusable). `nest4096` checked in
    # TAP_SCHEMA on 2026-10-20; 300 of 300 sampled rows carry the NESTED order-12 pixel of
    # their position (the column's TAP_SCHEMA description says "Ring scheme", which is wrong).
    adapter: adl-healpix
    adapter_params:
      table: ukidss_dr11plus.lassource

# Crossmatch: the radius a table of positions is matched within, and what it rests on.
crossmatch:
  radius: 1 arcsec
  radius_note: >-
    DR1 median seeing 0.82 arcsec; astrometric rms 50-100 mas tied to 2MASS (Lawrence et al.
    2007, arXiv:astro-ph/0604426, Table 2). These are DR1 values; no DR11 document was
    opened. Value set by the author (HG2, 2026-10-19); the instrument-based proposal was 0.5
    arcsec.

catalog_filters:
  ukidss11: >-
    ukidss11_mag_aper3_k <= 18.2
    OR (ukidss11_mag_aper3_k IS NULL AND ukidss11_mag_aper3_h <= 18.8)
    OR (ukidss11_mag_aper3_k IS NULL AND ukidss11_mag_aper3_h IS NULL AND ukidss11_mag_aper3_j <= 19.6)
  ukidss11_note: >-
    5 sigma point source in a 2 arcsec aperture, VEGA on the WFCAM system,
    to match the photometry above (Lawrence et al. 2007, LAS): YJHK
    20.2/19.6/18.8/18.2. K is the shallowest, and is WFCAM's K rather than
    VIRCAM's Ks -- a different passband with a different Vega offset.

cutout:
  - adapter: sia          # VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-25, IVOA registry
    adapter_params:
      service_url: http://wfaudata.roe.ac.uk/ukidssdr11-siap/
      bands: Y,J,H,K        # WFCAM spelling; the columns are y/j/h/k
    bands: [y, j, h, k]
    enabled: false

photometric_system:
  filters:
    y: UKIRT/UKIDSS.Y
    j: UKIRT/UKIDSS.J
    h: UKIRT/UKIDSS.H
    k: UKIRT/UKIDSS.K
  vega_offsets:
    # UKIRT/WFCAM (Hewett et al. 2006). The -0.080 mag Y zero-point
    # correction introduced at UKIDSS DR3 is already folded into the released
    # DR11 magnitudes, so it must NOT be applied again here.
    y: 0.634
    j: 0.938
    h: 1.379
    k: 1.900
  measurements:
    - system: vega_mag
      apertures: [aper3, petro, hall]
  pixel_unit: unknown
  pixel_unit_note: As ukidss10 -- WFCAM frames carry a per-image MAGZPT.

# UKIDSS DR11 Large Area Survey source table: near-infrared YJHK photometry
# over the northern UKIDSS footprint.
# Table: ukidss_dr11plus.lassource (Astro Data Lab TAP)
# Crossmatched spatially against target_candidates on (ra, dec).
#
# Magnitudes are VEGA, on the WFCAM system. WFCAM's K is not VIRCAM's Ks
# (vhs5) -- different passband, different Vega-to-AB offset -- so the band is
# spelled `k` here and `ks` there.
#
# Aperture tokens follow the WFAU naming: `aper3` is apermag3, the 2.0 arcsec
# aperture-corrected magnitude recommended for point sources; `petro` is the
# Petrosian magnitude; `hall` is the total (Hall) magnitude. VHS publishes no
# `hall` family, which is the one schema difference between the two surveys.
column_mapping:
  sourceid: 'id'                   # UID of this merged detection, assigned by the merge algorithm
  ra: 'ra'                         # right ascension, J2000, deg
  dec: 'dec'                       # declination, J2000, deg

  yapermag3: 'mag_aper3_y'                # default point-source Y aperture-corrected mag (2.0 arcsec diam), Vega mag
  yapermag3err: 'mag_aper3_y_err'         # error on default point/extended-source Y mag, mag
  japermag3: 'mag_aper3_j'                # default point-source J aperture-corrected mag (2.0 arcsec diam), Vega mag
  japermag3err: 'mag_aper3_j_err'         # error on default point/extended-source J mag, mag
  hapermag3: 'mag_aper3_h'                # default point-source H aperture-corrected mag (2.0 arcsec diam), Vega mag
  hapermag3err: 'mag_aper3_h_err'         # error on default point/extended-source H mag, mag
  kapermag3: 'mag_aper3_k'                # default point-source K aperture-corrected mag (2.0 arcsec diam), Vega mag
  kapermag3err: 'mag_aper3_k_err'         # error on default point/extended-source K mag, mag

  ypetromag: 'mag_petro_y'                # extended-source Y mag (Petrosian), Vega mag
  ypetromagerr: 'mag_petro_y_err'         # error on ypetromag, mag
  jpetromag: 'mag_petro_j'                # extended-source J mag (Petrosian), Vega mag
  jpetromagerr: 'mag_petro_j_err'         # error on jpetromag, mag
  hpetromag: 'mag_petro_h'                # extended-source H mag (Petrosian), Vega mag
  hpetromagerr: 'mag_petro_h_err'         # error on hpetromag, mag
  kpetromag: 'mag_petro_k'                # extended-source K mag (Petrosian), Vega mag
  kpetromagerr: 'mag_petro_k_err'         # error on kpetromag, mag

  yhallmag: 'mag_hall_y'                  # total (Hall) Y mag, Vega mag
  yhallmagerr: 'mag_hall_y_err'           # error on yhallmag, mag
  jhallmag: 'mag_hall_j'                  # total (Hall) J mag, Vega mag
  jhallmagerr: 'mag_hall_j_err'           # error on jhallmag, mag
  hhallmag: 'mag_hall_h'                  # total (Hall) H mag, Vega mag
  hhallmagerr: 'mag_hall_h_err'           # error on hhallmag, mag
  khallmag: 'mag_hall_k'                  # total (Hall) K mag, Vega mag
  khallmagerr: 'mag_hall_k_err'           # error on khallmag, mag

  mergedclass: 'class'                    # class flag: 1|0|-1|-2|-3|-9 = galaxy|noise|star|probableStar|probableGalaxy|saturated
  mergedclassstat: 'class_stat'           # merged N(0,1) stellarness-of-profile statistic
  pstar: 'p_star'                         # probability that the source is a star
  pgalaxy: 'p_galaxy'                     # probability that the source is a galaxy
  pnoise: 'p_noise'                       # probability that the source is noise
  psaturated: 'p_saturated'               # probability that the source is saturated

  priorsec: 'primary'                    # seam code for a unique (=0) or duplicated (!=0) source
  ebv: 'ebv'                              # galactic dust extinction from Schlegel maps, mag

  ypperrbits: 'errbits_y'         # additional WFAU post-processing error bits, Y
  jpperrbits: 'errbits_j'         # additional WFAU post-processing error bits, J
  hpperrbits: 'errbits_h'         # additional WFAU post-processing error bits, H
  kpperrbits: 'errbits_k'         # additional WFAU post-processing error bits, K
```

### Schema of this file

| Key present | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `survey_slug` | str | yes | — | Canonical lowercase identifier for the survey and default column prefix. |
| `name` | str | yes | — | Human-readable survey and data-release name used in logs, plans, and reports. |
| `catalog` | list of catalog entries | no | [] | Remote or local catalogues queried for target extraction or crossmatching. |
| `crossmatch` | mapping | no | None | How a table of positions is matched against this survey. Required for a survey with an `lsdb` catalog; `crossmatch` null removes it, and a survey without it takes no part in `mosaics-crossmatch`. |
| `catalog_filters` | mapping (prefix -> SQL expression or note) | no | {} | Post-hoc DuckDB SQL quality/depth/redshift cuts applied during production (nulls failing survey columns without dropping the row). |
| `cutout` | list of cutout entries | no | [] | Image cutout backends (`hips`, `lsv`, `nersc`, `sia`, `vsa`) serving this survey's passbands. |
| `photometric_system` | mapping | no | None | Passband SVO filter identifiers, flux/magnitude homogenisation rules, and image pixel calibration. |
| `column_mapping` | mapping (remote_column -> alias) | no | {} | Projection and column renaming applied when crossmatching against this survey's photometric catalogue. The loader adds the catalog's prefix to every alias, or the hosted survey's for the columns under its `provides` key. |

### Adapter parameters

**Catalogue `ukidss11` (`adapter: adl-healpix`):**

| Parameter | Allowed Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `table` | str | — | Fully qualified table on Astro Data Lab that carries a HEALPix NESTED index column (e.g. `gaia_dr3.gaia_source`, `allwise.source`, `ls_dr11.tractor`). |
| `service` | str | `datalab` (the public TAP at `https://datalab.noirlab.edu/tap`, no login) | A full TAP endpoint or a shorthand of the TAP services, for a test archive. |
| `remote_ra_column` | str | found by UCD (`pos.eq.ra`), then by name | Remote right ascension column name (`mean_fiber_ra` for `desi_dr1.zpix`). |
| `remote_dec_column` | str | found by UCD (`pos.eq.dec`), then by name | Remote declination column name. |
| `index_column` | str | `nest4096` | The table's HEALPix NESTED index. Its values are checked against the returned positions on the first query of every run. |
| `index_order` | int | 12 (the order of `nest4096`) | The HEALPix order of `index_column`. |
| `max_rows_per_query` | int | 50000 | Most rows one query may return. A query whose result reaches it is split and asked again, never truncated. |
| `max_ranges_per_query` | int | 50 | Most index ranges one query may carry. The public TAP times out well above this (probed at 100 and 500). |
| `rows_per_deg2` | float | None (counted by a few `COUNT(*)` queries) | The table's mean source density per square degree. When given, the planner sends no counting query. |

- **Cutout `None` (`adapter: sia`, bands `['y', 'j', 'h', 'k']`):** configured `adapter_params`: `service_url='http://wfaudata.roe.ac.uk/ukidssdr11-siap/'`, `bands='Y,J,H,K'`.

### Common changes

- **Disable catalogue crossmatching**: To omit `ukidss11` catalogue matching in a composite pipeline run, set `enabled: false` on the catalogue entry in your entrypoint YAML:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/ukidss11:
      catalog:
        - name: ukidss11
          enabled: false
  ```
- **Relax or disable depth filters**: To alter or remove the default 5-sigma point-source selection filter on aperture magnitudes, override `catalog_filters`:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/ukidss11:
      catalog_filters:
        ukidss11: null
  ```
- **Enable WFAU SIA image cutouts**: To retrieve FITS image cutouts directly from WFAU Edinburgh, enable the SIA adapter and specify target passbands:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/ukidss11:
      cutout:
        - adapter: sia
          adapter_params:
            service_url: http://wfaudata.roe.ac.uk/ukidssdr11-siap/
            bands: Y,J,H,K
          bands: [y, j, h, k]
          enabled: true
  ```

## Data served by the archive

- **Catalogue archive vs cutouts**: In `mosaics`, `ukidss11` queries the DR11plus LAS source catalogue hosted on the NSF NOIRLab Astro Data Lab TAP service (`ukidss_dr11plus.lassource`). In contrast, `ukidss9` accesses DR9 photometry via CDS HATS Parquet partitions using LSDB, and `ukidss10` defines active SIA cutouts from WFAU Edinburgh.
- **Vega system and WFCAM passbands**: Magnitudes are published in the Vega system on the UKIRT WFCAM photometric system. To convert to AB magnitudes, apply the Hewett et al. (2006) offsets: $Y: +0.634$, $J: +0.938$, $H: +1.379$, $K: +1.900$ mag.
- **WFCAM K vs VIRCAM Ks**: WFCAM's $K$ filter is physically distinct from VIRCAM's $K_s$ filter (`vhs5`, `viking`) and 2MASS $K_s$. They have different bandpass profiles and Vega-to-AB offsets (WFCAM $K$ offset is $+1.900$ mag; VIRCAM $K_s$ offset is $+1.839$ mag). In `mosaics`, the passband is designated `k` for UKIDSS and `ks` for VISTA surveys.
- **Y-band zero-point calibration**: The $-0.080$ mag $Y$-band zero-point correction introduced at UKIDSS DR3 is already incorporated into released DR11 magnitudes and must not be reapplied.
- **Image pixel units and zero points**: WFCAM frames carry a per-image zero point (`MAGZPT` in FITS headers); no single survey-wide calibration factor exists, so `pixel_unit` is marked as `unknown`.
- **Aperture naming conventions**: `aper3` corresponds to `y/j/h/kAperMag3` (2.0 arcsec diameter aperture-corrected magnitude for point sources), `petro` corresponds to Petrosian magnitudes, and `hall` represents total (Hall) magnitudes. VHS publishes no `hall` family, which is the primary schema difference between UKIDSS and VHS.
- **Point-source depth cut**: The default catalogue filter requires $K \le 18.2$ mag (or $H \le 18.8$ mag, or $J \le 19.6$ mag if $K$ is null), reflecting 5-sigma point-source completeness in a 2 arcsec aperture (Lawrence et al. 2007).

# UKIDSS LAS DR9 (`ukidss9`)

<!-- generated:survey-page -->
The UKIDSS Data Release 9 (DR9) Large Area Survey (LAS) is an 82,655,526-row near-infrared photometric catalogue covering the northern and equatorial sky across the $Y, J, H, K$ passbands. Observed with the Wide Field Camera (WFCAM) on the 3.8-metre United Kingdom Infrared Telescope (UKIRT) on Maunakea, LAS provides wide-area near-infrared photometry complementing northern optical surveys.

In `mosaics`, `ukidss9` serves as a local photometric catalogue source using the `lsdb` adapter to crossmatch against CDS-hosted HATS partitioned Parquet files (VizieR catalogue `II/319/las9`) with a precomputed 34-arcsec margin cache (`border12_34arcsec`). This allows client-side spatial matching without uploading candidate coordinates to remote services. Extracted columns include aperture-corrected 2.0 arcsec magnitudes (`aper3`), Petrosian magnitudes (`petro`), and total Hall magnitudes (`hall`), alongside profile classification statistics and duplicate flags.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| What MOSAICS extracts | Catalogue: `ukidss9` (photometric, `lsdb`) |
| Archives | HATS (`vizcat.cds.unistra.fr`) |
| Bands / wavelength range | `y` (`UKIRT/UKIDSS.Y`), `j` (`UKIRT/UKIDSS.J`), `h` (`UKIRT/UKIDSS.H`), `k` (`UKIRT/UKIDSS.K`) |
| Used by | `mosaics-targets` (crossmatch), `mosaics-crossmatch` |
| Crossmatch radius | `1` arcsec. As ukidss11: DR1 median seeing 0.82 arcsec and astrometric rms 50-100 mas (Lawrence et al. 2007, arXiv:astro-ph/0604426, Table 2); no DR9 document was opened. Value set by the author (HG2, 2026-10-19); the instrument-based proposal was 0.5 arcsec. |

### The shipped file

Source: `defs/surveys/ukidss9.yaml`

```yaml

#
# The targets pipeline's UKIDSS, and a different data release from `ukidss11`.
# DR11PLUS is served by Astro Data Lab and by WFAU and by no HATS server, while
# LAS DR9 is VizieR II/319, which CDS publishes as HATS -- so this survey is
# matched on this machine instead of being uploaded to Data Lab. A different
# release is a different prefix, so nothing downstream can mistake these
# columns for DR11's.
#
# Photometry only: `ukidss11.yaml` keeps the cutouts, which are DR11 imaging.

survey_slug: ukidss9
name: UKIDSS LAS DR9

catalog:
  - name: ukidss9
    type: photometric
    adapter: lsdb
    adapter_params:
      # VizieR II/319 (las9), HATS at CDS: 82,655,526 rows.
      path: https://vizcat.cds.unistra.fr/hats/ukidss_dr9_las/main
      # The collection's default margin, a 34-arcsec halo.
      margin_cache: https://vizcat.cds.unistra.fr/hats/ukidss_dr9_las/border12_34arcsec

# Crossmatch: the radius a table of positions is matched within, and what it rests on.
crossmatch:
  radius: 1 arcsec
  radius_note: >-
    As ukidss11: DR1 median seeing 0.82 arcsec and astrometric rms 50-100 mas (Lawrence et
    al. 2007, arXiv:astro-ph/0604426, Table 2); no DR9 document was opened. Value set by the
    author (HG2, 2026-10-19); the instrument-based proposal was 0.5 arcsec.

photometric_system:
  filters:
    y: UKIRT/UKIDSS.Y
    j: UKIRT/UKIDSS.J
    h: UKIRT/UKIDSS.H
    k: UKIRT/UKIDSS.K
  vega_offsets:
    # UKIRT/WFCAM (Hewett et al. 2006), as for ukidss11. The -0.080 mag Y
    # zero-point correction introduced at UKIDSS DR3 is already folded into
    # the DR9 magnitudes, so it must NOT be applied again here.
    y: 0.634
    j: 0.938
    h: 1.379
    k: 1.900
  measurements:
    - system: vega_mag
      apertures: [aper3, petro, hall]

# over the northern UKIDSS footprint.

# column it relabels.
#
# Magnitudes are VEGA, on the WFCAM system. WFCAM's K is not VIRCAM's Ks
# (vhs5) -- different passband, different Vega-to-AB offset -- so the band is
# spelled `k` here and `ks` there.
#
# The LAS observes J twice. II/319 publishes both epochs; the first is the one
# carried, since it is the one every J family below has.
#
# Aperture tokens follow the WFAU naming, as in ukidss11: `aper3` is apermag3,
# the 2.0 arcsec aperture-corrected magnitude recommended for point sources;
# `petro` is the Petrosian magnitude; `hall` is the total (Hall) magnitude.
# II/319 publishes no E(B-V), no pSaturated and no priOrSec; `m` is its
# duplicate flag instead.
column_mapping:

  RAJ2000: 'ra'                    # right ascension, J2000, deg, at Epoch (ra)
  DEJ2000: 'dec'                   # declination, J2000, deg, at Epoch (dec)

  e_pYmag: 'mag_petro_y_err'          # error on pYmag (yPetroMagErr), mag
  pJmag1: 'mag_petro_j'               # Petrosian J magnitude, first epoch (j_1PetroMag), Vega mag
  e_pJmag1: 'mag_petro_j_err'         # error on pJmag1 (j_1PetroMagErr), mag
  pHmag: 'mag_petro_h'                # Petrosian H magnitude (hPetroMag), Vega mag
  e_pHmag: 'mag_petro_h_err'          # error on pHmag (hPetroMagErr), mag
  pKmag: 'mag_petro_k'                # Petrosian K magnitude (kPetroMag), Vega mag
  e_pKmag: 'mag_petro_k_err'          # error on pKmag (kPetroMagErr), mag

  pG: 'prob_galaxy'                  # probability that the source is a galaxy (pGalaxy)
  pN: 'prob_noise'                   # probability that the source is noise (pNoise)
  m: 'duplicate'                     # 2 marks a duplicated source, 1 a unique one

  Yflags: 'errbits_y'                # WFAU post-processing error bits, Y (yppErrBits)
  Jflags1: 'errbits_j'               # WFAU post-processing error bits, J first epoch (j_1ppErrBits)
  Hflags: 'errbits_h'                # WFAU post-processing error bits, H (hppErrBits)
  Kflags: 'errbits_k'                # WFAU post-processing error bits, K (kppErrBits)
```

### Common changes

- **Disable catalogue crossmatching**: To disable `ukidss9` catalogue matching in an entrypoint configuration, set `enabled: false`:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/ukidss9:
      catalog:
        - name: ukidss9
          enabled: false
  ```
- **Redirect to a local HATS mirror**: If the HATS dataset has been mirrored locally, update the directory path and margin cache:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/ukidss9:
      catalog:
        - name: ukidss9
          adapter: lsdb
          adapter_params:
            path: /path/to/local/hats/ukidss_dr9_las/main
            margin_cache: /path/to/local/hats/ukidss_dr9_las/border12_34arcsec
  ```
- **Filter duplicate detections**: To retain only unique sources and exclude duplicate detections in overlapping frames, add a post-hoc filter:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/ukidss9:
      catalog_filters:
        unique_only: "ukidss9_duplicate == 1"
  ```

## Data served by the archive

- **Local HATS vs remote TAP**: `ukidss9` matches against CDS's HATS partitioning of VizieR catalogue II/319 (82,655,526 rows) via LSDB on the local machine. This is distinct from `ukidss11`, which performs remote TAP queries against Astro Data Lab. The columns are mapped with the prefix `ukidss9_*` so downstream analyses cannot confuse them with DR11 data.
- **Column mapping from VizieR II/319**: Column names in `ukidss9.yaml` map directly from VizieR II/319 ReadMe labels (`Ymag`, `Jmag1`, `Hmag`, `Kmag`, `pYmag`, `Ytot`, `cl`, `m`) to `ukidss9_*` fields.
- **Multi-epoch J band**: The UKIDSS LAS observed the $J$ band twice. VizieR II/319 publishes both epochs (`Jmag1` and `Jmag2`). In `ukidss9.yaml`, the first epoch (`Jmag1`, `pJmag1`, `Jtot1`, `e_Jmag1`, `Jflags1`) is selected because it is uniformly available across all aperture measurement families (`aper3`, `petro`, `hall`).
- **Missing columns relative to WFAU DR11**: VizieR II/319 does not publish galactic extinction $E(B-V)$, `pSaturated`, or seam codes (`priOrSec`). Duplicate status is tracked via the flag `m`, where 1 denotes a unique source and 2 denotes a duplicate.
- **Vega system and WFCAM passbands**: Magnitudes are in the Vega system on the UKIRT WFCAM system. Apply Hewett et al. (2006) offsets to convert to AB: $Y: +0.634$, $J: +0.938$, $H: +1.379$, $K: +1.900$ mag. The $-0.080$ mag $Y$-band zero-point correction from DR3 is already incorporated into DR9. WFCAM's $K$ band is not VIRCAM's $K_s$ band.
- **Cutouts**: `ukidss9` is a catalogue-only survey in `mosaics`. Near-infrared image cutouts are handled by `ukidss10` or `ukidss11`.

# UNIONS DR5 (`unions`)

<!-- generated:survey-page -->
The Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS) is a collaborative deep imaging survey of the northern sky conducted by the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope (CFHT) and the Panoramic Survey Telescope and Rapid Response System (Pan-STARRS). The CFHT component, known as the Canada-France Imaging Survey (CFIS), supplies deep optical imaging—most notably in $u$ and $r$ bands—using MegaCam on the 3.6-metre CFHT on Maunakea. UNIONS Data Release 5 (DR5) represents a key public milestone for this high-resolution northern dataset.

In `mosaics`, `unions` is configured as a cutout-only survey entry. Currently, it serves as an explicit architectural placeholder for CFIS/UNIONS $r$-band imaging (`CDS/P/UNIONS/DR5/r`) with `enabled: false`.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| What MOSAICS extracts | Cutouts: `hips` (color) |
| Archives | CDS HiPS / hips2fits (`alasky.cds.unistra.fr`), `tapvizier.cds.unistra.fr` |
| Bands / wavelength range | `color` |
| Used by | `mosaics-cutout full` |

## Configuration

### The shipped file

Source: `defs/surveys/unions.yaml`

```yaml
# UNIONS DR5 -- cutouts only, HiPS tiles, r band.

survey_slug: unions
name: UNIONS DR5

cutout:
  - adapter: hips
    # DOES NOT RESOLVE. Kept so the survey is described rather than
    # forgotten, and so the next person does not re-derive the same
    # guess. `--plan` will not reach it: the adapter is disabled. No
    # single-band sibling exists either -- see the note below -- so
    # `color` is the only key this survey has.
    adapter_params:
      hips_id: CDS/P/UNIONS/DR5/r
    bands: [color]
    enabled: false

photometric_system:
  pixel_unit: unknown
  pixel_unit_note: >-
    Moot, because there are no tiles. no HiPS matching UNIONS or CFIS is registered (MOCServer, 2026-09-04). The
    pixel unit cannot be resolved for a service that does not exist, and
    this entry is a record of having looked rather than a working adapter.
    Whoever finds a real HiPS for this survey -- or another cutout service
    -- should replace the adapter below and revisit this note; the tiles
    would then need a scale check of their own, as no HiPS build this
    project has seen states one.
```

### Common changes

- **Retain disabled state**: In normal operation, leave the cutout adapter disabled (`enabled: false`) because no public HiPS tiles are currently served for UNIONS on CDS MOCServer.
- **Enable an alternate cutout endpoint**: If a working private or institutional HiPS service or custom cutout adapter becomes available, configure its parameters in an entrypoint YAML:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/unions:
      cutout:
        - adapter: hips
          adapter_params:
            hips_id: CDS/P/UNIONS/DR5/r
            service_url: https://your-hips-service.org/
          bands: [color]
          enabled: true
  ```
- **Omit survey from cutout planning**: To prevent `unions` from appearing in cutout planning runs:


## Data served by the archive

- **Disabled HiPS status**: As of 2026-09-04, no HiPS dataset matching UNIONS or CFIS is registered on the CDS MOCServer (`CDS/P/UNIONS/DR5/r` does not resolve). The entry in `defs/surveys/unions.yaml` is retained in a disabled state (`enabled: false`) to document the survey configuration and prevent redundant investigations into missing endpoints.
- **Pipeline planning**: When running `mosaics-cutout` with `--plan`, the adapter is bypassed because `enabled: false` is respected by the pipeline generator, avoiding failing network requests.
- **Bands and pixel units**: The survey definition specifies band `[color]` because no single-band sibling HiPS exists. The pixel unit is declared as `unknown` because physical pixel scale and photometric calibration cannot be established without accessible image tiles. If an active endpoint is integrated in the future, the tile scale and zero point must be verified independently.

# unWISE NEO11 (`unwise`)

<!-- generated:survey-page -->
unWISE provides unblurred, full-sky coadded imaging from NASA's Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) and the NEOWISE reactivation mission. Unlike the standard AllWISE atlas images, unWISE preserves the native angular resolution of the WISE telescope without spatial smoothing or low-pass filtering. The NEO11 coadd data release incorporates eleven years of spaceborne survey observations in the mid-infrared W1 (3.4 µm) and W2 (4.6 µm) channels.

In `mosaics`, `unwise` serves as an image cutout survey delivering mid-infrared W1 and W2 FITS stamps via the Legacy Survey Viewer (`lsv` adapter with `layer: unwise-neo11`). Cutout pixel fluxes are calibrated in nanomaggies ($1\,\mathrm{nanomaggy} = 3.631\,\mu\mathrm{Jy}$, equivalent to an AB zero point of 22.5 mag).

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| What MOSAICS extracts | Cutouts: `lsv` (w1,w2), `hips` (w1), `hips` (w2) |
| Archives | Legacy Survey Viewer (`legacysurvey.org`), CDS HiPS / hips2fits (`alasky.cds.unistra.fr`), `datalab.noirlab.edu` |
| Bands / wavelength range | `w1`, `w2` |
| Used by | `mosaics-cutout full` |

## Configuration

### The shipped file

Source: `defs/surveys/unwise.yaml`

```yaml
# unWISE NEO11 coadds -- the cutouts.
#
# A reprocessing of WISE imaging, and a different data product from the AllWISE
# catalogue the `wise` definition describes.
#
# The `unwise_*` photometry columns are NOT declared here: they come from the
# Legacy Survey DR11 tractor table, which carries unWISE forced photometry in
# the same rows as its optical fluxes, and defs/surveys/ls11.yaml describes
# them under `provides.unwise`. One query, so one description, in the file
# whose query it is. This file is the imaging. The depth cut on that
# photometry is `catalog_filters.unwise` in ls11.yaml, moved there with it.

survey_slug: unwise
name: unWISE NEO11

cutout:
  - adapter: lsv          # VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-25
    adapter_params:
      layer: unwise-neo11
      bands: W1,W2          # comma form: band names are two characters
    bands: [w1, w2]
  # The same two bands as single-band HiPS with FITS tiles (MOCServer,
  # 2026-09-05). Note the keys are the *column* tokens, lowercased, while
  # the stack's plane order keeps the archive's `W1`/`W2` spelling.
  # Disabled: these are a different coadd generation from `unwise-neo11`,
  # so `pixel_unit: nanomaggy` -- a statement about the Viewer -- has not
  # been checked against them.
  - adapter: hips
    adapter_params:
      hips_id: CDS/P/unWISE/W1
    bands: [w1]
    enabled: false
  - adapter: hips
    adapter_params:
      hips_id: CDS/P/unWISE/W2
    bands: [w2]
    enabled: false

photometric_system:
  pixel_unit: nanomaggy
  pixel_unit_note: unWISE coadds are served in nanomaggies by the Legacy Survey Viewer.
  # No `borrow_filters` any more: `unwise` has photometry of its own now --
  # hosted by ls11 -- so the registry finds `unwise_w1` directly and a borrow
  # from `wise` would only be a second, quieter way to reach the same
  # WISE/WISE.W1 curve. Two routes to one answer is how they start to
  # disagree.
```

### Schema of this file

| Key present | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `survey_slug` | str | yes | — | Canonical lowercase identifier for the survey and default column prefix. |
| `name` | str | yes | — | Human-readable survey and data-release name used in logs, plans, and reports. |
| `cutout` | list of cutout entries | no | [] | Image cutout backends (`hips`, `lsv`, `nersc`, `sia`, `vsa`) serving this survey's passbands. |
| `photometric_system` | mapping | no | None | Passband SVO filter identifiers, flux/magnitude homogenisation rules, and image pixel calibration. |

### Adapter parameters

- **Cutout `None` (`adapter: lsv`, bands `['w1', 'w2']`):** configured `adapter_params`: `layer='unwise-neo11'`, `bands='W1,W2'`.
- **Cutout `None` (`adapter: hips`, bands `['w1']`):** configured `adapter_params`: `hips_id='CDS/P/unWISE/W1'`.
- **Cutout `None` (`adapter: hips`, bands `['w2']`):** configured `adapter_params`: `hips_id='CDS/P/unWISE/W2'`.

### Common changes

- **Disable unWISE cutouts**: To omit unWISE cutouts from a composite pipeline run:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/unwise:
      cutout: []
  ```
- **Filter to a single band**: To request only W1 cutouts from the Legacy Survey Viewer:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/unwise:
      cutout:
        - adapter: lsv
          adapter_params:
            layer: unwise-neo11
            bands: W1
          bands: [w1]
  ```
- **Enable CDS HiPS cutouts**: To use CDS HiPS FITS tiles instead of the Viewer:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/unwise:
      cutout:
        - adapter: hips
          adapter_params:
            hips_id: CDS/P/unWISE/W1
          bands: [w1]
          enabled: true
  ```

## Data served by the archive

- **Cutouts vs forced photometry**: In `mosaics`, `defs/surveys/unwise.yaml` configures cutouts only. unWISE forced photometry is not declared here; it is extracted as part of the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys DR11 query (`defs/surveys/ls11.yaml` under `provides.unwise`). This query measures unWISE fluxes at optical target positions, yielding `unwise_*` columns (`unwise_flux_w1`, `unwise_flux_ivar_w1`, `unwise_rchisq_w1`, `unwise_fracflux_w1`, etc.) in AB nanomaggies.
- **unWISE AB fluxes vs AllWISE Vega magnitudes**: Do not confuse `unwise` forced photometry with standalone AllWISE photometry from `defs/surveys/wise.yaml`. AllWISE publishes profile-fit Vega magnitudes (`wise_mag_w1`, etc.). In contrast, `unwise` forced photometry is already on the AB scale ($m_\mathrm{AB} = 22.5 - 2.5 \log_{10}(\mathrm{nanomaggy})$). Applying AllWISE Vega-to-AB offsets to `unwise` fluxes is an error.
- **Cutout backend and pixel calibration**: The active cutout adapter queries the `unwise-neo11` layer from the Legacy Survey Viewer in nanomaggies (`pixel_unit: nanomaggy`). Secondary CDS HiPS adapters (`CDS/P/unWISE/W1`, `CDS/P/unWISE/W2`) represent an earlier coaddition generation and are disabled by default (`enabled: false`) because their pixel scale and calibration differ from the Viewer.
- **Filter definitions**: `borrow_filters` is omitted from `unwise.yaml` because the filter registry resolves `unwise_w1` directly from `ls11.yaml`'s `provides.unwise` definition (`WISE/WISE.W1`), preventing duplicate filter paths.

# VISTA Hemisphere Survey DR5 (`vhs5`)

<!-- generated:survey-page -->
The VISTA Hemisphere Survey Data Release 5 (VHS DR5) is a wide-field near-infrared astronomical survey covering approximately 18,000 deg² of the southern celestial hemisphere in the $Y, J, H, K_s$ passbands. Observations were conducted using the VISTA InfraRed CAMera (VIRCAM) mounted on the ESO 4.1-metre Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy (VISTA) at Cerro Paranal, Chile. The survey reaches a nominal 5-sigma point-source depth of $K_s \sim 18.2$ mag (Vega) across its standard survey footprint.

In `mosaics`, `vhs5` provides near-infrared catalogue crossmatching and FITS image cutouts across the southern sky. Catalogue crossmatching is executed locally via the `lsdb` adapter against CDS HATS partitioned Parquet tables (VizieR catalogue `II/367/vhs_dr5`, comprising 1,374,207,485 rows in 3,132 partitions) using a precomputed 34-arcsec margin cache (`border12_34arcsec`). Image cutouts in $Y, J, H, K_s$ are retrieved using the `vsa` adapter querying the VISTA Science Archive (VSA) Simple Image Access (SIA) service hosted by WFAU Edinburgh.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| What MOSAICS extracts | Catalogue: `vhs5` (photometric, `lsdb`); Cutouts: `vsa` (y,j,h,ks) |
| Archives | HATS (`vizcat.cds.unistra.fr`), VSA (`wfaudata.roe.ac.uk`) |
| Bands / wavelength range | `y` (`Paranal/VISTA.Y`), `j` (`Paranal/VISTA.J`), `h` (`Paranal/VISTA.H`), `ks` (`Paranal/VISTA.Ks`) |
| Used by | `mosaics-targets` (crossmatch), `mosaics-cutout full`, `mosaics-crossmatch` |
| Crossmatch radius | `1` arcsec. No seeing figure in the DR5 release description (a figure only); astrometric rms about 0.15 arcsec per coordinate against 2MASS (ESO release description, Sect. 4.2). The radius rests on that figure alone. |

## Configuration

### The shipped file

Source: `defs/surveys/vhs5.yaml`

```yaml
# VISTA Hemisphere Survey DR5 -- photometry and cutouts.

survey_slug: vhs5
name: VISTA Hemisphere Survey DR5

catalog:
  - name: vhs5
    type: photometric
    adapter: lsdb
    adapter_params:
      # VHS DR5 as VizieR II/367, HATS at CDS: 1,374,207,485 rows in 3,132
      # partitions, matched on this machine rather than uploaded to Data Lab.
      path: https://vizcat.cds.unistra.fr/hats/vhs_dr5/
      # A 34-arcsec halo carrying every column the map below names (checked
      # 2026-09-13).
      margin_cache: https://vizcat.cds.unistra.fr/hats/vhs_dr5/border12_34arcsec

# Crossmatch: the radius a table of positions is matched within, and what it rests on.
crossmatch:
  radius: 1 arcsec
  radius_note: >-
    No seeing figure in the DR5 release description (a figure only); astrometric rms about
    0.15 arcsec per coordinate against 2MASS (ESO release description, Sect. 4.2). The
    radius rests on that figure alone.

catalog_filters:
  vhs5: vhs5_mag_aper3_ks <= 18.2
  vhs5_note: >-
    5 sigma point source over the standard survey area, VEGA on the VIRCAM
    system, to match the photometry above (McMahon et al. 2013). AB would be
    18.2 + 1.84 = 20.0. Ks is the shallowest of the four bands, so it is what
    decides whether an object is in the imaging. No H/J fallback: unlike
    ukidss11's LAS, McMahon et al. 2013 gives VHS's H and J depths only as a
    mean over the combined images (and shallower still in the partial-H
    regions), not the single survey-wide number the other cascades in this
    file rest on, so a value here would be less trustworthy than leaving the
    row unfilled.

cutout:
  - adapter: vsa          # VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-25, IVOA registry
    adapter_params:
      service_url: http://wfaudata.roe.ac.uk/vista-siap/
      bands: Y,J,H,Ks       # VIRCAM spelling; the columns are y/j/h/ks
    bands: [y, j, h, ks]
    cost:
      latency_s: 2.0
      bandwidth_bps: 15000000
      concurrency: 2
      render_seconds: 0.3

photometric_system:
  filters:
    # VIRCAM. Its Ks is not WFCAM's K, nor 2MASS's Ks.
    y: Paranal/VISTA.Y
    j: Paranal/VISTA.J
    h: Paranal/VISTA.H
    ks: Paranal/VISTA.Ks
  vega_offsets:
    # CASU-recommended (Gonzalez-Fernandez et al. 2018).
    y: 0.618
    j: 0.937
    h: 1.384
    ks: 1.839
  measurements:
    - system: vega_mag
      apertures: [aper3, petro]
  pixel_unit: unknown
  pixel_unit_note: >-
    VSA frames carry a per-image MAGZPT, so one survey-wide number would be
    wrong by however much the frames differ. This stays unknown on purpose;
    a per-image calibration would have to read each frame's own header.

# VISTA Hemisphere Survey (VHS) DR5 catalogue: near-infrared YJHKs
# photometry over the southern-hemisphere VHS footprint.
# Catalogue: VizieR II/367 (McMahon et al. 2020), HATS at CDS, matched with
# LSDB. The names are VizieR's labels from the II/367 ReadMe; each comment
# names the WFAU column it relabels, which is what the aliases were first
# written against.
#
# Magnitudes are VEGA, on the VIRCAM system. Note VIRCAM's Ks is not WFCAM's K
# (ukidss11) and not 2MASS's Ks either -- the three carry different Vega-to-AB
# offsets, which is why the band is spelled `ks` here and `k` in ukidss11.
#
# Aperture tokens follow the WFAU naming: `aper3` is apermag3, the 2.0 arcsec
# aperture-corrected magnitude recommended for point sources; `petro` is the
# Petrosian magnitude recommended for extended sources.
column_mapping:
  SrcID: 'id'                  # unique ID of this merged detection (sourceID)
  RAJ2000: 'ra'                # right ascension, J2000, deg (ra)
  DEJ2000: 'dec'               # declination, J2000, deg (dec)

  Yap3: 'mag_aper3_y'          # default point source Y mag, 2.0 arcsec aperture corrected (yAperMag3), Vega mag
  e_Yap3: 'mag_aper3_y_err'     # error on Yap3 (yAperMag3Err), mag
  Jap3: 'mag_aper3_j'          # default point source J mag, 2.0 arcsec aperture corrected (jAperMag3), Vega mag
  e_Jap3: 'mag_aper3_j_err'     # error on Jap3 (jAperMag3Err), mag
  Hap3: 'mag_aper3_h'          # default point source H mag, 2.0 arcsec aperture corrected (hAperMag3), Vega mag
  e_Hap3: 'mag_aper3_h_err'     # error on Hap3 (hAperMag3Err), mag
  Ksap3: 'mag_aper3_ks'        # default point source Ks mag, 2.0 arcsec aperture corrected (ksAperMag3), Vega mag
  e_Ksap3: 'mag_aper3_ks_err'     # error on Ksap3 (ksAperMag3Err), mag

  Ypmag: 'mag_petro_y'          # extended source Y mag, Petrosian (yPetroMag), Vega mag
  e_Ypmag: 'mag_petro_y_err'     # error on Ypmag (yPetroMagErr), mag
  Jpmag: 'mag_petro_j'          # extended source J mag, Petrosian (jPetroMag), Vega mag
  e_Jpmag: 'mag_petro_j_err'     # error on Jpmag (jPetroMagErr), mag
  Hpmag: 'mag_petro_h'          # extended source H mag, Petrosian (hPetroMag), Vega mag
  e_Hpmag: 'mag_petro_h_err'     # error on Hpmag (hPetroMagErr), mag
  Kspmag: 'mag_petro_ks'        # extended source Ks mag, Petrosian (ksPetroMag), Vega mag
  e_Kspmag: 'mag_petro_ks_err'     # error on Kspmag (ksPetroMagErr), mag

  # mergedClass spans [-3, 1] in DR5: 1|0|-1|-2|-3 = galaxy|noise|star|
  # probableStar|probableGalaxy. II/367 publishes no pSaturated, so the
  # vhs5_p_saturated column the Data Lab table fed is gone.
  Mclass: 'class'               # class flag (mergedClass)
  Mstat: 'class_stat'           # merged N(0,1) stellarness-of-profile statistic (mergedClassStat)
  pStar: 'p_star'               # probability that the source is a star (pStar)
  pGal: 'p_galaxy'              # probability that the source is a galaxy (pGalaxy)
  pNoise: 'p_noise'             # probability that the source is noise (pNoise)

  PriOrSec: 'priorsec'          # seam code for a unique (=0) or duplicated (!=0) source (priOrSec)
  E(B-V): 'ebv'                 # galactic dust extinction from Schlegel maps, mag (eBV)
  prim: 'primary'        # flag marking primary sources (=1) vs. duplicates (=0) (primary_source)

  Yperrbits: 'errbits_y'        # additional WFAU post-processing error bits, Y (yppErrBits)
  Jperrbits: 'errbits_j'        # additional WFAU post-processing error bits, J (jppErrBits)
  Hperrbits: 'errbits_h'        # additional WFAU post-processing error bits, H (hppErrBits)
  Ksperrbits: 'errbits_ks'      # additional WFAU post-processing error bits, Ks (ksppErrBits)
```

| Key present | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `survey_slug` | str | yes | — | Canonical lowercase identifier for the survey and default column prefix. |
| `name` | str | yes | — | Human-readable survey and data-release name used in logs, plans, and reports. |
| `catalog` | list of catalog entries | no | [] | Remote or local catalogues queried for target extraction or crossmatching. |

| `column_mapping` | mapping (remote_column -> alias) | no | {} | Projection and column renaming applied when crossmatching against this survey's photometric catalogue. The loader adds the catalog's prefix to every alias, or the hosted survey's for the columns under its `provides` key. |

### Common changes

- **Disable or relax depth filters**: To alter or remove the default 5-sigma point-source selection filter ($K_s \le 18.2$ mag):
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/vhs5:
      catalog_filters:
        vhs5: null
  ```
- **Disable cutouts**: To perform catalogue crossmatching without fetching image cutouts:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/vhs5:
      cutout: []
  ```
- **Select specific cutout passbands**: To download only a subset of bands (e.g. $J$ and $K_s$):
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/vhs5:
      cutout:
        - adapter: vsa
          bands: [j, ks]
          adapter_params:
            bands: J,Ks
  ```
- **Redirect to a local HATS mirror**: When working with a local mirror of the HATS partition cache:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/vhs5:
      catalog:
        - name: vhs5
          adapter: lsdb
          adapter_params:
            path: /path/to/local/hats/vhs_dr5/
            margin_cache: /path/to/local/hats/vhs_dr5/border12_34arcsec
  ```

## Data served by the archive

- **VIRCAM Ks vs WFCAM K and 2MASS Ks**: Magnitudes are in the Vega system on the ESO VISTA VIRCAM photometric system. VIRCAM's $K_s$ filter is distinct from UKIRT WFCAM's $K$ filter (`ukidss9`, `ukidss11`) and 2MASS $K_s$. The passband is explicitly designated `ks` in `vhs5` (Vega-to-AB offset $+1.839$ mag, Gonzalez-Fernandez et al. 2018) rather than `k` in UKIDSS ($+1.900$ mag).
- **Vega-to-AB offsets**: Official CASU-recommended Vega-to-AB offsets (Gonzalez-Fernandez et al. 2018) are: $Y: +0.618$, $J: +0.937$, $H: +1.384$, $K_s: +1.839$ mag.
- **Local HATS catalogue matching**: Matching operates locally against CDS's HATS partitioning of VizieR catalogue II/367 (1,374,207,485 rows, 3,132 partitions) via LSDB. Column aliases map from VizieR II/367 names (`Yap3`, `Jap3`, `Hap3`, `Ksap3`, `Ypmag`, `Mclass`, `prim`) to standardized `vhs5_*` identifiers.
- **Depth filter logic**: The default catalogue filter requires `vhs5_mag_aper3_ks <= 18.2` (5-sigma point source depth, Vega, McMahon et al. 2013). $K_s$ is the shallowest band and determines imaging presence. No $H$ or $J$ fallback is applied because McMahon et al. (2013) quotes $H$ and $J$ depths only as a mean over combined images rather than a uniform survey-wide threshold.
- **Apertures and schema differences with UKIDSS**: VHS publishes 2.0 arcsec aperture-corrected magnitudes (`aper3`) and Petrosian magnitudes (`petro`). Unlike UKIDSS, VHS publishes no total Hall (`hall`) magnitudes, and VizieR II/367 omits `pSaturated`.
- **Image cutout zero points**: VSA FITS images carry a per-image zero point (`MAGZPT` in FITS headers); no survey-wide calibration constant exists, so `pixel_unit` is designated `unknown`.

# VISTA Kilo-degree Infrared Galaxy Survey (`viking`)

<!-- generated:survey-page -->
The VISTA Kilo-degree Infrared Galaxy Survey (VIKING) is an intermediate-depth, near-infrared survey covering approximately 1,500 deg² of the extragalactic sky in two distinct stripes (one northern, one southern) in the $Z, Y, J, H, K_s$ passbands. Observations were conducted using VIRCAM on the ESO 4.1-metre VISTA telescope at Cerro Paranal, achieving 5-sigma point-source depths of $Z = 22.4$, $Y = 21.4$, $J = 20.9$, $H = 19.9$, and $K_s = 19.3$ mag (Vega). VIKING is roughly two magnitudes deeper than the wide-angle VHS over its selected footprint.

In `mosaics`, `viking` provides near-infrared image cutouts across its five passbands (`z, y, j, h, ks`) via the `vsa` adapter querying the VISTA Science Archive (VSA) Simple Image Access endpoint (`http://wfaudata.roe.ac.uk/vista-siap/`). Because it shares the VSA service URL with `vhs5`, it is shipped in a disabled state (`enabled: false`) to avoid redundant simultaneous requests.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| What MOSAICS extracts | Cutouts: `vsa` (z,y,j,h,ks) |
| Archives | VSA (`wfaudata.roe.ac.uk`), `tapvizier.cds.unistra.fr` |
| Bands / wavelength range | borrows passbands from `vhs5` |
| Used by | `mosaics-cutout full` |

## Configuration

### The shipped file

Source: `defs/surveys/viking.yaml`

```yaml
# VIKING -- cutouts only. Shares the VISTA SIA service with vhs5.

survey_slug: viking
name: VISTA Kilo-degree Infrared Galaxy Survey

# max_mag: 20.9 (max_mag_band: j). 5 sigma point source, VEGA, as vhs5: ZYJHKs
# 22.4/21.4/20.9/19.9/19.3. Roughly two magnitudes deeper than VHS over a far
# smaller footprint, which is the trade the two VISTA surveys make.
cutout:
  - adapter: vsa
    adapter_params:
      service_url: http://wfaudata.roe.ac.uk/vista-siap/
      bands: Z,Y,J,H,Ks     # VIRCAM spelling; the columns are z/y/j/h/ks
    bands: [z, y, j, h, ks]
    enabled: false        # same service as vhs5; enable one of the two

photometric_system:
  pixel_unit: unknown
  pixel_unit_note: As vhs5 -- VSA frames carry a per-image MAGZPT.
  borrow_filters: vhs5        # VIRCAM, the same passbands vhs5 lists
```

### Common changes

- **Enable VIKING cutouts**: To retrieve deeper VIKING cutouts instead of VHS across the VIKING footprint, enable the cutout adapter:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/viking:
      cutout:
        - adapter: vsa
          adapter_params:
            service_url: http://wfaudata.roe.ac.uk/vista-siap/
            bands: Z,Y,J,H,Ks
          bands: [z, y, j, h, ks]
          enabled: true
  ```
- **Filter to specific bands**: To request only a subset of passbands (e.g. $Z, J, K_s$):
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/viking:
      cutout:
        - adapter: vsa
          bands: [z, j, ks]
          adapter_params:
            bands: Z,J,Ks
  ```
- **Disable cutouts**: To ensure VIKING is excluded from cutout planning:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/viking:
      cutout: []
  ```

## Data served by the archive

- **Relationship to VHS**: Both VIKING and VHS observe with VIRCAM on the ESO 4.1m VISTA telescope and query the same VISTA Science Archive Simple Image Access service at WFAU Edinburgh (`http://wfaudata.roe.ac.uk/vista-siap/`). Whereas VHS prioritizes wide southern coverage (~18,000 deg² to $K_s \sim 18.2$), VIKING reaches roughly two magnitudes deeper ($K_s \sim 19.3$, $J \sim 20.9$, $Z \sim 22.4$) over a targeted ~1,500 deg² footprint.
- **Mutual exclusivity in default configuration**: Because `vhs5` and `viking` query the same underlying VSA cutout service, `viking.yaml` ships with `enabled: false` ("enable one of the two"). Researchers targeting fields in the VIKING footprint can enable `viking` and disable `vhs5`.
- **Filter definitions and Vega offsets**: VIKING borrows its photometric filter definitions from `vhs5` (`borrow_filters: vhs5`), using the VIRCAM passbands and CASU Vega-to-AB offsets (Gonzalez-Fernandez et al. 2018): $Y: +0.618$, $J: +0.937$, $H: +1.384$, $K_s: +1.839$ mag. VIRCAM $K_s$ is not WFCAM $K$.
- **Image pixel units and calibration**: Cutout pixel units are marked as `unknown` because individual VSA FITS images carry per-image zero points (`MAGZPT` in FITS headers) without a survey-wide constant calibration factor.

# AllWISE (`wise`)

<!-- generated:survey-page -->
The AllWISE Source Catalog is a comprehensive full-sky mid-infrared astronomical catalogue containing 747,634,026 sources detected by NASA's Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE). It combines data from the 4-band cryogenic, 3-band cryo, and NEOWISE post-cryogenic survey phases in the W1 (3.4 µm), W2 (4.6 µm), W3 (12 µm), and W4 (22 µm) mid-infrared passbands.

In `mosaics`, `wise` serves as a standalone mid-infrared catalogue source, crossmatched through Astro Data Lab's TAP service against table `allwise.source`. The extraction provides profile-fit (PSF) Vega magnitudes (`wise_mag_w1` through `wise_mag_w4`), photometric errors, signal-to-noise ratios, reduced chi-squared fit metrics, blend flags, and per-band contamination/quality flags across all four WISE bands.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| What MOSAICS extracts | Catalogue: `wise` (photometric, `adl-healpix`) |
| Archives | `datalab.noirlab.edu` |
| Bands / wavelength range | `w1` (`WISE/WISE.W1`), `w2` (`WISE/WISE.W2`), `w3` (`WISE/WISE.W3`), `w4` (`WISE/WISE.W4`) |
| Used by | `mosaics-targets` (crossmatch), `mosaics-crossmatch` |
| Crossmatch radius | `3` arcsec. PSF FWHM 6.1, 6.8, 7.4 and 12.0 arcsec in W1-W4 (AllWISE Explanatory Supplement, I.2.a); positions of high signal-to-noise, unconfused sources accurate to about 50 mas (Sect. II.1). Value set by the author (HG2, 2026-10-19); the instrument-based proposal was 5 arcsec. |

## Configuration

### The shipped file

Source: `defs/surveys/wise.yaml`

```yaml
# AllWISE -- photometry.
#
# The catalogue, as distinct from `unwise`, which is a reprocessing of the same
# imaging into coadds this project takes cutouts from.

survey_slug: wise
name: AllWISE

catalog:
  - name: wise
    type: photometric
    # Astro Data Lab's public TAP, by ranges of the table's `nest4096` index: no login, no
    # upload; the rows that come back are a superset of the matches and the match itself is
    # made here by haversine separation (HG3, 2026-10-20: Data Lab accounts can no longer be
    # authenticated, so the `adl` upload route is unusable). `nest4096` checked in
    # TAP_SCHEMA on 2026-10-20.
    adapter: adl-healpix
    adapter_params:
      table: allwise.source

# Crossmatch: the radius a table of positions is matched within, and what it rests on.
crossmatch:
  radius: 3 arcsec
  radius_note: >-
    PSF FWHM 6.1, 6.8, 7.4 and 12.0 arcsec in W1-W4 (AllWISE Explanatory Supplement, I.2.a);
    positions of high signal-to-noise, unconfused sources accurate to about 50 mas (Sect.
    II.1). Value set by the author (HG2, 2026-10-19); the instrument-based proposal was 5
    arcsec.

photometric_system:
  filters:
    # The same passbands as ls11's W1-W4, but Vega magnitudes rather than AB
    # nanomaggies.
    w1: WISE/WISE.W1
    w2: WISE/WISE.W2
    w3: WISE/WISE.W3
    w4: WISE/WISE.W4
  vega_offsets:
    # The team's own values, recorded in Tractor headers as WISEAB1-4. SVO's
    # zero points imply 2.673/3.313/5.148/6.594 -- uniformly 0.026 mag lower,
    # a different Vega spectrum normalisation rather than a mismatched
    # passband. The team's values are used because they are what the surveys
    # calibrated against, and what ls11's already-AB W1-W4 were converted
    # with.
    w1: 2.699
    w2: 3.339
    w3: 5.174
    w4: 6.620
  measurements:
    - system: vega_mag
      apertures: [default]

# AllWISE source catalogue: mid-infrared W1-W4 profile-fit photometry.
# Table: allwise.source (Astro Data Lab TAP)
# Crossmatched spatially against target_candidates on (ra, dec).
#
# `mpro` is the profile-fit (PSF) magnitude and is the only photometry family
# taken from AllWISE, so the aperture token is omitted: `wise_mag_w1`, not
# `wise_mag_pro_w1`.
#
# Magnitudes are VEGA. This is the standalone AllWISE photometry -- do NOT
# confuse it with ls11's W1-W4, which are unWISE forced photometry already
# converted to AB by the Legacy Survey pipeline. Applying the Vega-to-AB
# offsets to those a second time is the most common error in multi-survey work.
column_mapping:
  designation: 'id'            # sexagesimal source name, the AllWISE identifier
  ra: 'ra'                     # right ascension, J2000, deg
  dec: 'dec'                   # declination, J2000, deg
  # sigra: 'ra_err'            # uncertainty in the right ascension, arcsec
  # sigdec: 'dec_err'          # uncertainty in the declination, arcsec

  w1mpro: 'mag_w1'             # W1 profile-fit magnitude, Vega mag
  w1sigmpro: 'mag_w1_err'      # error on the W1 profile-fit magnitude, mag
  w1snr: 'snr_w1'              # W1 signal-to-noise ratio
  w1rchi2: 'chi2_w1'           # reduced chi-squared of the W1 profile fit
  w2mpro: 'mag_w2'             # W2 profile-fit magnitude, Vega mag
  w2sigmpro: 'mag_w2_err'      # error on the W2 profile-fit magnitude, mag
  w2snr: 'snr_w2'              # W2 signal-to-noise ratio
  w2rchi2: 'chi2_w2'           # reduced chi-squared of the W2 profile fit
  w3mpro: 'mag_w3'             # W3 profile-fit magnitude, Vega mag
  w3sigmpro: 'mag_w3_err'      # error on the W3 profile-fit magnitude, mag
  w3snr: 'snr_w3'              # W3 signal-to-noise ratio
  w3rchi2: 'chi2_w3'           # reduced chi-squared of the W3 profile fit
  w4mpro: 'mag_w4'             # W4 profile-fit magnitude, Vega mag
  w4sigmpro: 'mag_w4_err'      # error on the W4 profile-fit magnitude, mag
  w4snr: 'snr_w4'              # W4 signal-to-noise ratio
  w4rchi2: 'chi2_w4'           # reduced chi-squared of the W4 profile fit

  w1sat: 'sat_w1'              # fraction of W1 pixels that are saturated
  w2sat: 'sat_w2'              # fraction of W2 pixels that are saturated
  w3sat: 'sat_w3'              # fraction of W3 pixels that are saturated
  w4sat: 'sat_w4'              # fraction of W4 pixels that are saturated

  rchi2: 'chi2'                # reduced chi-squared of the joint profile fit
  nb: 'nb'                     # number of blend components fitted
  na: 'na'                     # active deblending flag
  cc_flags: 'cc_flags'         # per-band contamination and confusion flags
  ext_flg: 'ext_flg'           # extended source flag
  var_flg: 'var_flg'           # per-band variability flags
  ph_qual: 'ph_qual'           # per-band photometric quality flags
  moon_lev: 'moon_lev'         # per-band fraction of frames affected by moonlight
  det_bit: 'det_bit'           # bitwise per-band detection flag
```

### Common changes

- **Disable catalogue crossmatching**: To omit AllWISE catalogue crossmatching in an entrypoint configuration:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/wise:
      catalog:
        - name: wise
          enabled: false
  ```
- **Filter on photometric quality**: To retain only unblended, high signal-to-noise sources with clean photometric quality flags in W1 and W2:
  ```yaml
  overrides:
    surveys/wise:
      catalog_filters:
        clean_w1w2: "wise_ph_qual LIKE 'AA%' AND wise_sat_w1 == 0 AND wise_sat_w2 == 0"
  ```
- **Modify crossmatch parameters**: To adjust spatial crossmatch search radius or join constraints, override `catalog[0].adapter_params` in your entrypoint YAML.

## Data served by the archive

- **Standalone AllWISE vs unWISE forced photometry**: AllWISE provides standalone, profile-fit (PSF) magnitudes in the Vega system derived from WISE coadded atlas images. In contrast, `unwise` forced photometry is delivered via the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys DR11 pipeline (`provides.unwise` in `defs/surveys/ls11.yaml`) in AB nanomaggies at optical source positions. Researchers must never apply AllWISE Vega-to-AB offsets to `unwise` fluxes, which are already on the AB system ($m_\mathrm{AB} = 22.5 - 2.5 \log_{10}(\mathrm{nanomaggy})$).
- **Photometry family**: Only profile-fit magnitudes (`w*mpro`) are extracted from `allwise.source`; aperture photometry is omitted. Consequently, column aliases omit aperture tokens (e.g. `wise_mag_w1`, `wise_mag_w1_err`).
- **Vega-to-AB zero-point offsets**: Official AllWISE team values (recorded in Tractor headers as WISEAB1–4) are: $W1: +2.699$, $W2: +3.339$, $W3: +5.174$, $W4: +6.620$ mag. These offsets are preferred over theoretical SVO zero points (which differ by a uniform $-0.026$ mag due to Vega spectrum normalisation) because they match the calibration used across legacy survey reductions.
- **Quality and blending indicators**: The catalogue provides essential diagnostics including photometric quality (`wise_ph_qual`), number of blend components (`wise_nb`), active deblending (`wise_na`), contamination/confusion flags (`wise_cc_flags`), and fractional moonlight contamination (`wise_moon_lev`), which should be consulted to filter blended or spurious sources.
- **Cutouts**: `wise` is a catalogue-only survey in `mosaics`. Mid-infrared image cutouts are handled by `unwise` using unblurred NEO11 coadds.

# Post-Hoc Reports

Every `mosaics` pipeline that produces a scientific catalogue or comparison dataset can render a structured **scireport bundle** describing what the run built, what failed, what had to be type-cast, what it asked of each astronomical archive, and how the resulting dataset passes scientific quality checks.

## The Four Reports

| Report Subcommand | Template ID | Input | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`mosaics-report targets`](../cli/reports.md#mosaics-report-targets) | `mosaics-targets@1` | `targets_report.yaml` (written automatically by `mosaics-targets run` / `production`) | Complete multi-chapter scientific and operational report on a 5-stage `targets` run: executive summary, overview, per-stage funnel and coverage chapters, scientific assessment (redshift consistency, photometry distributions, sky coverage), conclusion, and reproducibility manifest. |
| [`mosaics-report crossmatch`](../cli/reports.md#mosaics-report-crossmatch) | `mosaics-crossmatch@1` | `<output-stem>.crossmatch.yaml` (written automatically by `mosaics-crossmatch run`) | Crossmatch report: one chapter per survey with its radius and what it rests on, the overview, input profile, angular separation and multiplicity distributions, MOC footprint filter efficiency, output column definitions, archive request ledger, conclusion, and full remote table schema appendix. |
| [`mosaics-report compare_stamps`](../cli/reports.md#mosaics-report-compare_stamps) | `mosaics-compare-stamps@1` | Two cutout Lance datasets (`--left`, `--right`) | Pixel-for-pixel comparison of two cutout datasets (for example, `hips` service vs `hips --local`, or `lsv` vs `nersc`): eleven composite diagnostic figures with tidy per-stamp metric sidecars. |
| [`mosaics-report db_constraints`](../cli/reports.md#mosaics-report-db_constraints) | `mosaics-db-constraints@1` | `--config` entrypoint YAML | Standalone live-archive audit that measures how many rows each SQL constraint in a survey's `target_selection` query removes. |

## Output Layout

When a report renders into an output directory (`report/` by default next to the run's YAML summary), it leaves four artefacts:

```text
report/
├── <name>.scireport.zip     # Sealed, self-contained scireport bundle (manifest, tables, figures, numbers)
├── md/                      # Markdown chapters and tables for LLM agents and quick inspection
│   ├── index.md
│   └── chapters/
├── pdf/                     # Typeset PDF report for human readers (unless --no-report-pdf is passed)
│   └── <name>.pdf
└── render-manifest.json     # Build metadata and rendered file inventory
```

## Reading Reports with LLM Agents

The `md/` directory inside `report/` contains clean, chapter-by-chapter Markdown where every metric, check verdict, and summary table is rendered in plain text. Coding agents and research assistants can read `report/md/index.md` and the chapter files under `report/md/chapters/` directly without parsing PDFs or large binary catalogues.

## Re-rendering and Exporting with `scireport`

Because `<name>.scireport.zip` is a standard sealed `scireport` bundle, you can re-render it on any machine where `mosaics` (which registers the `mosaics-*` templates) and `scireport` are installed—or re-render a `targets_report.yaml` / `<output-stem>.crossmatch.yaml` file via `mosaics-report`:

```bash
# Re-render a targets run YAML without PDF generation
uv run -m mosaics.cli.report targets -r /data/targets/targets_report.yaml \
  -o /data/targets/report \
  --no-pdf

# Re-render a crossmatch run account
uv run -m mosaics.cli.report crossmatch -r /data/xmatch/matched.crossmatch.yaml \
  -o /data/xmatch/report
```


# Using This Documentation with an LLM Agent

This documentation site is published in both human-readable HTML and machine-readable Markdown so that LLM coding agents, research assistants, and automated scripts can inspect `mosaics` CLI flags, survey configurations, and upstream archive data models without scraping HTML.

## Machine-Readable Endpoints

Every page on this site has a plain-Markdown twin, and the site root publishes two index files following the `llms.txt` standard:

- **[`llms.txt`](https://nmcardoso.github.io/mosaics-docs/llms.txt)** — Concise index of every documentation page with its title and direct `.md` URL. Point an agent here first so it can discover which page answers a question without loading the entire documentation into context.
- **[`llms-full.txt`](https://nmcardoso.github.io/mosaics-docs/llms-full.txt)** — Single-file concatenation of the complete documentation in Markdown. Useful for long-context models or offline indexing.
- **Per-page `.md` twins** — Replace `.html` with `.md` on any page URL (or append `index.md` to directory URLs) to fetch the raw Markdown source of that page, including all generated CLI tables, configuration schemas, and survey data-model tables:
  - [`for-agents.md`](for-agents.md) (this page in Markdown)
  - [`surveys/index.md`](surveys/index.md) (the survey capability matrix)
  - `surveys/<slug>.md` (for example, [`surveys/ls11.md`](surveys/ls11.md), [`surveys/desi1.md`](surveys/desi1.md), [`surveys/lsstdp2.md`](surveys/lsstdp2.md))
  - `cli/<command>.md` (for example, [`cli/cutout.md`](cli/cutout.md), [`cli/targets.md`](cli/targets.md), [`cli/spectrum.md`](cli/spectrum.md))
  - [`configuration/index.md`](configuration/index.md) (complete YAML schema and adapter parameter tables)

## Step-by-Step Workflow for Agents

When asked to design, configure, or debug a `mosaics` data extraction run, an LLM agent should follow this sequence:

### 1. Discover Available Surveys and Capabilities

Fetch [`surveys/index.md`](surveys/index.md) to inspect the **Survey Capability Matrix**. Identify which surveys provide:
- `targets` stage-1 selection (`spectroscopic` or `photometric`),
- stage-3 photometric or stage-4 spectroscopic `catalog` crossmatching,
- `cutout` imaging stamps (and which backend: `hips`, `lsv`, or `nersc`),
- `spectrum` 1D spectra (`url`, `template`, `sparcl`, or `desi-healpix`).

### 2. Inspect Survey Schemas and Shipped YAML/SQL

For each survey `<slug>` involved in the user's task, fetch `surveys/<slug>.md` (for example, [`surveys/euclidq1.md`](surveys/euclidq1.md) or [`surveys/ls11.md`](surveys/ls11.md)). Each survey page contains:
- The **exact shipped YAML configuration** (`defs/surveys/<slug>.yaml`) and any **SQL query** (`defs/sql/<slug>.sql`).
- The **Source Data Models** table listing every column in the upstream archive table, its data type, physical unit, UCD, whether `mosaics` selects it by default, and what prefixed column name (`{prefix}<col>`) it maps to in the output dataset.

### 3. Construct or Customise a Configuration File

If the user needs additional archive columns, tighter quality constraints, or a subset of surveys:
1. Check [`configuration/index.md`](configuration/index.md) for the exact allowed keys in each section (`catalog`, `catalog_filters`, `column_mapping`, `cutout`, `spectra`, `target_selection`) and `adapter_params`.
2. Remember the strict loader rules:
   - Write the aliases in `column_mapping` **without** a prefix: the loader adds the survey's (`{slug}_`, or `{slug}p_` / `{slug}s_` when a survey defines both photometric and spectroscopic catalogues), so `ra: ra` gives `{slug}_ra`. An alias that already starts with the prefix raises. Columns of a hosted survey go under a key named after its `provides` prefix.
   - Unknown keys or invalid enum values (`pixel_unit`, `magnitude_system`, `wavelength_frame`, `error_representation`) will fail validation immediately.

### 4. Select the Right CLI Command and Flags

Fetch the relevant CLI reference page before proposing commands:
- **Cutouts:** [`cli/cutout.md`](cli/cutout.md) (`mosaics-cutout hips`, `lsv`, `nersc`, `full`, `peek`).
- **Spectra:** [`cli/spectrum.md`](cli/spectrum.md) (`mosaics-spectrum fetch`, `discover`, `full`, `peek`).
- **Queries:** [`cli/query.md`](cli/query.md) (`mosaics-query cone`, `region`, `download`, `sql`, `sweep`, `ssa`).
- **Targets Pipeline:** [`cli/targets.md`](cli/targets.md) (`mosaics-targets run`, `selection`, `ls11`, `photometric`, `spectroscopic`, `production`, `report`).
- **Crossmatch:** [`cli/crossmatch.md`](cli/crossmatch.md) (`mosaics-crossmatch run`, `moc`, `jobs`, `kill`, `del`): a table of positions against any survey that has a `crossmatch` section, including the Rubin/LSST Data Previews. Concepts: [`concepts/crossmatch.md`](concepts/crossmatch.md); Astro Data Lab without a login (`adl-healpix`, the adapter of `wise`, `gaia3` and `ukidss11`): [`concepts/datalab-healpix.md`](concepts/datalab-healpix.md).
- **Field of view:** [`cli/fov.md`](cli/fov.md) (`mosaics-fov`): add the cutout size that frames each galaxy to any table with the Legacy Survey shape and `r` magnitude; `mosaics-crossmatch run --fov SURVEY` does the same after a match, and `--hle` (on `mosaics-fov`, `mosaics-crossmatch run --fov` and `mosaics-targets`) chooses the half-light-ellipse method alone; `mosaics-cutout --default-fov` sizes the targets whose `fov` is empty. How it is computed: [`concepts/field-of-view.md`](concepts/field-of-view.md).
- **HiPSCat:** [`cli/hipscat.md`](cli/hipscat.md) (`mosaics-hipscat convert`, `import`, `crossmatch`, `info`, `validate`).
- **Distributed Proxy:** [`cli/proxy.md`](cli/proxy.md) (`mosaics-proxy up`, `serve`, `worker`, `status`, `down`).
- **Reports:** [`cli/reports.md`](cli/reports.md) (`mosaics-report targets`, `crossmatch`, `compare-stamps`, `db-constraints`).

Always include `--resume` on long-running extraction commands (`cutout`, `spectrum`, `targets`) so interrupted runs continue cleanly from their unique `--key-column`.

### 5. Verify Outputs and Inspect Reports

After a run finishes:
- Check [`data-model/reading-outputs.md`](data-model/reading-outputs.md) for Python recipes to read Lance cutout/spectrum datasets, distinguish failed rows (`null`) from empty spectra (`[]`), and inspect `<dataset>.failures.parquet`.
- If the pipeline generated a `report/md/` folder, read `report/md/index.md` and `report/md/chapters/*.md` to verify row counts, filter funnels, and scientific assessment checks.
